Thomas Müller’s penalty secured a 1-1 draw for the Vancouver Whitecaps against LAFC on the team’s return to BC Place Stadium. Son Heung-min had fired the visitors ahead with a neat turn and shot, but Müller won and converted a 76th-minute spot-kick after he was hauled down in the box by defender Yevhen Cheberko.

Brandon Bye scored the winning goal in the 82nd minute as the Portland Timbers handed the Seattle Sounders their sixth straight loss. Kevin Kelsey also scored for the Timbers, who are undefeated in four games after this 2-1 win. Kalani Kossa-Rienzi scored for the Sounders, who are dealing with a spate of injuries.

Sports.title: Transfer news: Welbeck joins Chelsea, Brentford complete record Sangaré deal
Sports.content:
Chelsea have signed Brighton’s veteran striker Danny Welbeck in a deal worth a reported £5m. Welbeck has agreed a two-year contract and will link up with Xabi Alonso’s squad on their pre-season tour.

The 35-year-old’s move to Stamford Bridge is a break from Chelsea’s policy of signing younger players with the potential to be developed. It is the first time they have paid a transfer fee for a player over the age of 26 since they signed Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang from Barcelona in 2022 when the striker was 33.

“When you hear of interest from Chelsea, it’s something that fills you with such immense pride. Knowing the history of Chelsea, it’s a club that wants to win trophies and is pushing to do that every single season,” Welbeck said.

“I’m really honoured to come to a club of this stature at what feels like a really exciting time. I know a few of the boys already and I’ve had fantastic conversations with the manager and already feel that connection. I’ve got that fire in my belly and I’m ready to give it everything for this club to make everyone at Chelsea, and the supporters, proud.”

Alonso was keen to add experience to his squad after last season’s disappointing 10th-place finish in the Premier League. He opted for Welbeck after the former Manchester United and Arsenal forward enjoyed a memorable campaign with Brighton.

Welbeck, who has 42 caps for England, scored 13 goals in 37 Premier League games last term after netting 10 times in 2024-25.

Welbeck’s arrival in west London will raise questions about the future of Chelsea striker Liam Delap, who signed from Ipswich last season, as well as fellow forwards Nicolas Jackson and Marc Guiu.

Welbeck is the latest player to move from Brighton to Chelsea in recent years after João Pedro, Moisés Caicedo, Robert Sánchez and Marc Cucurella, who joined Real Madrid earlier this summer.

Chelsea spent a British record £117m to sign the England forward Morgan Rogers, 24, from Aston Villa in July. They also secured the France defender Maxence Lacroix, 26, from Crystal Palace for £52m earlier this week and signed Atalanta defender Marco Palestra, 21, for £43m.

Brentford seal record Sangaré deal

Brentford have signed the Mali international Mamadou Sangaré from ⁠Lens for a club-record fee, reported to be £39m. Sangaré, 24, joins Brentford on a five-year contract, with ⁠the option to extend for another year.

“Mamadou ​is someone ‌that we’ve tracked ‌for quite some time. He’s been on ‌our radar and was a player we were really keen to bring in,” the Brentford head coach Keith Andrews said. “He’s a humble young man, but he’s equally as ⁠determined to succeed in his career. He ​fits ​everything we want from ​a Brentford player, on and ​off the ‌pitch.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sangaré left Austria’s Rapid Vienna to ‌join Lens last year, and featured prominently as they won the ​French Cup for the first time and finished second in Ligue 1.

View image in fullscreen Mamadou Sangaré has swapped RC Lens for Brentford in a £39m move. Photograph: Stéphanie Lecocq/Reuters

Bournemouth have announced the signing of António Silva from Benfica for a fee believed to be in the region of £25m. The 22-year-old defender becomes new manager Marco Rose’s second signing of the summer after the arrival of Álvaro Rodríguez earlier this week.

Silva made 235 senior appearances for Benfica and collected six major honours during his time in Portugal. He told the club website: “I am very happy to be here. It’s a pleasure to play for Bournemouth and in the Premier League.

“The mentality is always to win. I will try my best, and I will play for the fans. We have everything here that helps us perform on the pitch, and I can’t wait to get started.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane urged to consider Tottenham return in grovelling apology
Sports.content:
Could Harry Kane return to Tottenham this summer and try to break Alan Shearer's long-standing Premier League goal record?

Well, if the England captain ends up hearing talkSPORT host and Spurs fan Majestic's plea, he may end up considering it.

3 Kane has been told to consider a return to Tottenham this summer Credit: Getty

Kane's future has been widely spoken about, with his contract at Bayern Munich running out in the summer of 2027.

He has been attracting interest from Barcelona, while Chelsea have been tipped to make a potential move for him.

However, Bayern remain confident that the record-breaking striker will end up signing a new deal and talkSPORT understands that he is settled in Germany having spent the last three years there.

But could a return to Tottenham tempt him home?

Last month, talkSPORT commentator Ian Danter tipped Kane's England teammate Jude Bellingham to return to his boyhood club Birmingham City before he turns 30.

And Majestic used that example before setting out his plea for the 33-year-old to come back and play for his boyhood club Spurs.

'It's time to come home'

He began with a grovelling apology, saying: "Mr Harry Kane. I've apologised to you already before, as when you first left you broke my heart and I didn't want you to win anything. But Harry's won - he's a world-class striker.

"You've done it in Germany, you've won. I don't personally see Bayern winning the Champions League anytime soon, Arsenal are more likely to win it."

Then, Majestic sent a message directly to Bayern and Kane, looking down the camera in the talkSPORT studio and adding: "Bayern, you've had a great time with Harry, he's won you the league.

"We're going to give you the money back, so you will get £81million back, the release clause, bang, straight away, we'll trigger that.

3 Kane left Spurs after 14 years in 2023 as their all-time top goalscorer Credit: Getty

"Harry, come home. We'll give you £400,000 a week, big numbers, but he deserves it, a world superstar."

Majestic then went on to lay out a plan that Kane could follow in his bid to become the Premier League's all-time top goalscorer, as he still sits 47 goals behind Alan Shearer's record of 260 goals.

"Roberto De Zerbi says to him: 'Look, it's one season without European football, which allows you to have a bit more of a rest after a long season and a World Cup... it gives you the focus of scoring goals in the Premier League, you don't have to play in the League Cup," he continued.

"You are that close to Alan Shearer's record. If you have a good season this year, scoring 20+, which is very possible to do, you could become a Bundesliga champion, England's greatest goalscorer, Tottenham's greatest goalscorer and possibly the Premier League's greatest ever goalscorer.

"This is Harry Kane's legacy set in stone. People can't say he hasn't won anything, he's gone and done that. Now he can come home and push Spurs on.

"Come on Harry, it's time to come home, it's good for you, it's good for us, it's good for Bayern, let's do it."

3 Kane scored 280 goals for Spurs but never managed to win a trophy

Kane's record at Spurs

Kane left Tottenham in pursuit of a trophy and he's now done so - so could Majestic get his wish and see him return?

The 121-cap England international is Spurs' all-time top goalscorer, netting 280 goals in 435 appearances for the club.

He came through their academy in 2009 after five years in the set-up, playing for the first team over a 14-year period.

His incredible form in the Premier League was never rewarded with a title, but he has scored 213 goals in the top flight.

With Spurs, Kane also became the first player to score 100 away goals in the Premier League and beat Thierry Henry's record for the most goals in London derbies, among many other achievements.

Majestic mentioned his legacy and he certainly has one in North London - but could he add another chapter to his story?

Sports.title: Frank Lampard signs son of former England teammate, 18, on free transfer
Sports.content:
Frank Lampard signs son of former England teammate, 18, on free transfer

Coventry City have signed 18-year-old goalkeeper Jack Ruddy on a free transfer.

Ruddy will link up with Coventry's under-21 side five weeks after leaving Norwich U18s.

3 Lampard has been acquainted with Ruddy's dad during his playing career Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

3 Jack is the son of former Everton, Norwich, Wolves, Birmingham and Newcastle keeper John Credit: getty images

He is the son of former Premier League goalkeeper John Ruddy, who is best known for his time at Norwich. John also represented Wolves and Newcastle in the top flight.

The deal that sees Jack join Coventry was wrapped up last month, however, his mum and wife of John, Laura, confirmed the news on social media on Sunday.

Posting a picture of herself and Jack on the pitch at the CBS Arena, Laura said: "So proud of Jack for signing with Coventry City.

"The last five years haven’t always been easy, but you’ve never stopped working hard or believing in yourself.

"Seeing you smiling and enjoying your football again means everything."

Mates rates

Jack now calls one of his dad's former England teammates boss, with John and the Chelsea legend playing together for the Three Lions once.

That came in a 2-1 victory over Italy for the Three Lions in August 2012, which saw John come on for Jack Butland at half time.

Goals from Phil Jagielka and Jermain Defoe secured England a 2-1 win in Bern, Switzerland after Daniele De Rossi headed Italy in front.

This was Ruddy Sr's only appearance for the England national team with Lampard earning 106 caps.

John is yet to call time on his playing career at 39 years old, although he's currently without a club having left Newcastle upon the expiration of his contract in June.

Coventry mean business

The Sky Blues, who romped to last season's Championship title, have been busy in the transfer market as they gear up for their first appearance in the Premier League for 25 years.

Coventry have beaten their transfer record twice so far in the summer window, first paying £15.4million to land defender Aurele Amenda from Eintracht Frankfurt in early July.

But this record was eclipsed last week when they wrapped up the signing of goalkeeper Carl Rushworth from Brighton in a £22.5m deal.

Elsewhere, Coventry have forked out £20m to sign winger Loum Tchaouna from Burnley while also making midfielder Frank Onyeka's loan from Brentford a permanent transfer.

Lampard's men will need to hit the ground running as they face champions Arsenal in the 2026/27 Premier League season opener on Friday August 21.

They travel to Manchester City after their first home game of the season which sees Coventry entertain another of the promoted Championship clubs in Hull City.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta rules out exit for Arsenal star in four-word response to question
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta rules out exit for Arsenal star in four-word response to question

Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Viktor Gyokeres will not be leaving Arsenal this summer amid rumours of an exit.

Gyokeres, who signed for the Gunners last summer for £63.7million, had been linked to a potential swap deal for Julian Alvarez.

3 Gyokeres will be staying at Arsenal despite talk of a summer exit Credit: Getty

talkSPORT reported in July that the Premier League champions explored the possibility of offering their striker as a makeweight.

But nothing has developed in those talks as the transfer window rumbles on - and Arteta has now shut things down.

The Arsenal manager was asked a question on Gyokeres' future at the Emirates after his side's 4-1 win over Girona on Saturday.

And he definitively replied: "He’s going to stay."

Arteta was also asked whether he is still looking at Alvarez, replying: "I’m not going to talk about a footballer who isn’t ours."

So, Gyokeres is now confirmed to remain at Arsenal for the foreseeable future as he looks to build on his first season at the club.

The 28-year-old scored 14 Premier League goals in his maiden campaign, netting another five in the Champions League.

In total, he had a tally of 21 goals in 55 games for the Gunners, putting up some impressive numbers in all competitions.

However, there have still been some doubts raised over Gyokeres' overall performances and whether Arsenal could improve.

But that hasn't had an impact on Arteta, who is going to stick with his striker heading into the 2026/27 season.

3 Gyokeres helped Arsenal win the title in his first season, scoring 14 league goals Credit: Getty

Gyokeres stays, but who comes in?

As well as confirming that Gyokeres will stay at Arsenal this summer, Arteta also revealed he's looking at more new signings.

The Gunners have already signed Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, with the winger scoring on his debut against Girona.

Piero Hincapie has also signed on a permanent deal, with goalkeeper Illan Meslier joining on a free from Leeds.

But there could be plenty more business being done by the reigning champions, with two Brazilian stars linked.

Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes continues to get closer to a move to the Emirates Stadium, while a transfer saga involving a potential approach for Real Madrid superstar Vinicius Junior continues.

Arteta hasn't commented on those deals specifically, but he has said: "Well, we are really active, trying to improve and evolve the team. That's clear.

3 Arteta confirmed Gyokeres is staying and also hinted at some more signings Credit: Getty

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else. And you can just see the transfer market and our opponents.

"What we are doing, we won't sit still and we are very ambitious in what we want to do."

As for outgoings, Gyokeres won't be leaving, but Leandro Trossard has already departed the club this summer.

Trossard signed for Besiktas for £17million in mid-July.

The transfer window will close at 11pm on September 1.

Sports.title: Charlie Austin reveals first coaching job rejection at former club
Sports.content:
Charlie Austin reveals first coaching job rejection at former club

Charlie Austin has revealed that he was rejected by his former club QPR after applying for a coaching job.

The 37-year-old striker posted the disappointing news on social media as he missed out on working within QPR's academy.

2 Austin has been rejected after an interview for an academy coaching job at QPR Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Austin, who played 148 times and scored 61 goals across three spells with the Championship side, had an interview for the position.

He posted on X: "First job interview disappointment.

"Gutted not to progress to the next stage for @QPRAcademy coaching team. The club I really wanted to work with.

"Will keep working hard and hoping my time will come.

"Good luck to whoever lands the role, what a club you get to join!"

In reply to his post, a fan questioned whether Austin expected to get the coaching role as he previously played for QPR.

However, he made sure to shut those suggestions down, adding: "No hidden agenda. Just honest disappointment at missing out on a role at a club I think highly of.

"Nothing but respect for QPR, the process was fair and professional, everyone was great.

"As I said will keep working hard for my time to come! This just weren’t my time."

Austin has not yet taken a role in coaching, and his playing career is still ongoing with semi-pro club Hungerford Town.

2 Austin is hoping to take his first steps into football coaching Credit: Getty Images - Getty

Austin's goal-filled career

Austin is clearly looking for the next step in his career as he nears the end of his playing days at the age of 37.

The forward has played 218 times in the Championship and over 100 times in the Premier League since 2011.

As mentioned, he played 148 times for QPR, while he has also featured 133 times for Swindon Town, scoring 60 goals.

He made 90 appearances for Burnley too, netting 44 times.

Austin scored 31 times across his time with Southampton and West Brom, and also had a stint in Australia in 2022.

In total across his professional playing career, he scored exactly 200 goals in 510 games across all levels.

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League striker Victor Anichebe could buy fairytale EFL club
Sports.content:
Former Premier League striker Victor Anichebe is reportedly spearheading a bid to take over Bromley.

Anichebe is said to be leading talks to buy the newly-promoted League One club, amid their rise up the EFL.

2 Ex-Everton striker Anichebe is said to be leading talks over a potential takeover of Bromley Credit: Getty

Bromley have gone from the National League to the third tier of the English football pyramid in just two years.

Following promotion to League Two in 2024, they went on to get promoted to League One at the end of last season.

It's widely considered a fairytale story, as this will be their first ever campaign at this level - and now they could end up being taken over by an ex-Premier League star.

Anichebe is now locked in talks with Bromley owner Robin Stanton-Gleaves, according to The Sun. talkSPORT has contacted Bromley for comment.

The 38-year-old was also linked to a potential takeover of non-league side Gateshead last year.

But now, he could enter ownership at a higher level, with Bromley bosses said to understand that they need some extra cash to compete in League One.

It is reported that Anichebe is already having an impact on Bromley's summer recruitment ahead of a proposed takeover.

He is the owner of Lumira Group, who are 'a long-term holding company investing in sport, education, healthcare and infrastructure across the UK'.

The former Nigeria international was recently involved in a £20million proposal for a new leisure development in Liverpool.

And he could be closing in on becoming a football club owner for the first time as he spearheads his group in negotiations.

2 Bromley could be set to have an ex-Premier League star in charge of the club Credit: Getty

Bromley kickstart their 2026/27 campaign with a Carabao Cup first round tie against Reading on Saturday.

They then play their first ever League One match against Barnsley a week later on Saturday, August 15.

Anichebe's playing career

Anichebe has moved into the business side of sports since retiring from football in the summer of 2018.

But many fans will remember his days playing in the Premier League, where he made over 200 appearances.

He scored 27 goals and provided 12 assists across his spells with Everton, Sunderland and West Brom from 2006 to 2017.

The ex-forward spent the longest time at Everton, playing 168 times for the Toffees, scoring 26 goals in all competitions.

For West Brom, he netted nine times in 63 games, while for Sunderland, he scored three goals in 19 appearances.

On the international stage, Anichebe picked up 11 caps for Nigeria, scoring one goal for his country.

Sports.title: Vinicius Junior’s agency hit out at ‘fake and damaging’ reports in damning statement
Sports.content:
Vinicius Junior’s agency hit out at ‘fake and damaging’ reports in damning statement

Vinicius Junior's agency, Roc Nation, has hit out at 'fake and damaging' reports from the media this summer.

Roc Nation Sports International released a damning statement on Sunday amid reports linking Vinicius Jr. to Arsenal.



3 Vini Jr.'s agency has released a damning statement regarding media reporting Credit: Getty

The statement called on journalists to be more 'accountable' and slammed 'unprofessional and uninformed' behaviour.

However, it did not specifically mention Vini Jr.'s transfer saga.

Roc Nation's president, Michael Yormark, posted on Instagram: "Roc Nation Sports International and our entire team cannot stand idle when unprofessional and uninformed media publish fake and damaging information for attention-seeking purposes.

"This is especially unacceptable when it personally targets our clients without any foundation.



"It is disruptive, harmful and libellous. Media outlets and journalists need to hold themselves more accountable."

Roc Nation are an agency, founded by legendary music artist Jay-Z, that represents multiple sports stars across the world.



They work with many NFL players, including Saquon Barkley, as well as NBA stars like Kyrie Irving and LaMelo Ball.

As well as Vini Jr, they also represent incoming Real signing Yan Diomande, Gabriel Martinelli and Endrick among other footballers.



Vinicius Junior to Arsenal latest

It's not clear whether Roc Nation are speaking about Vinicius Jr. and the ongoing rumours surrounding a Real Madrid exit.

But fans are sure to try and connect the two, with the Brazilian still being linked to Premier League champions Arsenal.

3 Roc Nation posted the statement titled 'Fake News' but didn't mention Vini Jr. Credit: Instagram @michaelyormark

Vini Jr. is out of contract at Real next year, and talkSPORT understands talks are still ongoing over him signing a new deal.



Whilst that stand-off continues, the Gunners are contemplating making a move for the superstar winger.

Club-to-club talks are not yet underway though, and Jose Mourinho is understood to want to keep Vini Jr. at the Bernabeu.

The saga is sure to rumble on as the transfer window remains open and his contract talks remain ongoing.

Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta has even been asked about the links during the Gunners' pre-season campaign.



When asked, 'When's Vini joining?', Arteta smiled in reaction.

3 The Real Madrid superstar's contract runs out next summer and Arsenal are interested Credit: Getty

And he later said to reporters on whether he will be bringing in some more signings this summer: "Well, we are already active trying to improve and evolve the team – that's clear.

"We expect to have movements in the next few weeks, obviously, because we want to get better like anybody else, and you can just see the transfer market and our opponents what we are doing.

"We won't sit still and we are very ambitious what we want to do."

Sports.title: Chelsea complete signing of World Cup star on seven-year deal
Sports.content:
Valentin Barco has signed a seven-year contract at Chelsea to join from sister club Strasbourg.

The 22-year-old, who used to ply his trade at Brighton, completes his move to the Blues with the deal being agreed ahead of the summer.

2 Barco brings some Premier League experience on his return to England Credit: Getty

He initially signed for Strasbourg on loan from Brighton in February 2025, before completing a switch worth £8million in July of that year.

Barco made seven appearances for the Seagulls ahead of his transfer to France, where he worked under former Chelsea boss Liam Rosenior.

Chelsea have opted to press ahead with the deal despite Rosenior being sacked from his post.

Barco was part of Argentina's World Cup squad this summer, playing in their group stage victory over Jordan.

But as a midfielder, he could face plenty of competition at Stamford Bridge when he arrives later this year.

Moises Caicedo, Enzo Fernandez, Romeo Lavia and Dario Essugo are midfield options at the disposal of new manager Xabi Alonso.

However, Barco could have one less competitor amid the uncertainty over Fernandez and his future in west London.

Barco in, Fernandez out?

After Chelsea were thrashed 8-2 on aggregate by Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League in March, Fernandez criticised the club's board.

He said he didn't understand their decision to allow head coach Enzo Maresca to leave the club at the beginning of the year.

Fernandez then generated speculation over a move to Real Madrid as he admitted he would like to live in the Spanish capital.

2 Barco could end up replacing Fernandez should he leave the club Credit: Getty

talkSPORT understands he is open to a move to Madrid this summer, although the Spanish giants publicly denied their interest in Fernandez in July.

Fernandez was subsequently sanctioned for the comments having been prevented from playing Chelsea's FA Cup win over Port Vale in April, which finished 7-0 to Chelsea.

He was also not involved in their Premier League fixture away at Manchester City on April 12 as well.

Busy summer

Barco is the latest addition for Chelsea, which has seen them splash out on numerous summer signings.

They broke the transfer record for a British player with the £117million acquisition of England star Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Meanwhile, France centre-back Maxence Lacroix has joined in a £52m deal from Crystal Palace.

The Blues announced the signing of former Arsenal and Manchester United striker Danny Welbeck on a two-year deal.

And former Liverpool captain Jordan Henderson is set to complete his move to the west London club imminently.

Sports.title: Liverpool could make shock Curtis Jones U-turn despite on-field bust up with Dominik Szoboszlai
Sports.content:
Liverpool could make shock Curtis Jones U-turn despite on-field bust up with Dominik Szoboszlai

Liverpool may yet offer Curtis Jones a new contract at the club.

That's despite the midfielder's spat with teammate Dominik Szoboszlai.

2 Jones argued with Szoboszlai, seemingly upset at not being handed the captain's armband after the Hungarian was substituted against Wrexham Credit: X / @anythingLFC_

The pair clashed following Liverpool's pre-season win over Wrexham in New York, with fellow Reds players Kostas Tsimikas and Jeremie Frimpong stepping in to try and diffuse the situation.

Inter Milan are among the clubs interested in signing Jones but Liverpool are not dead set on offloading their academy graduate, reports Ben Jacobs.

Joining Shaun Custis and Henry Winter on talkSPORT, Jacobs explained: "Inter are pushing for Curtis Jones. They made an offer, in inverted commas – although Liverpool don’t really see it as a formal bid – in the region of €35million (approximately £29m) and that’s their third approach – €32million and €25million were the other numbers.

"And Jones would welcome a move to Inter. Liverpool want a minimum of €40m and in this inflated market, some people are even saying €50m.

"And yet, if the window shuts, we might get the opposite extreme, because Andoni Iraola’s said that he likes Curtis Jones – and despite the bust-up you mentioned, Liverpool are not averse to offering Jones a new deal if he stays.

"But my sense is Inter will be back and Liverpool are a bit frustrated by this because they don’t want it through intermediaries anymore.

"The perspective of the club, according to my info, is if Inter want Curtis Jones – a bit like Bruno Guimaraes, Newcastle-Arsenal – knock on our front door, make us a formal offer and then you might find a financial compromise.

"So, this is going to be one to watch in the month of August."

Jones has just under a year to run on his Liverpool contract, meaning he would be available on a free transfer next summer should he not sign an extension – a situation the Reds will want to avoid.

The six-cap England international has made over 200 appearances for his boyhood club since making his first-team debut shortly before his 18th birthday in January 2019.

2 Jones scored on his England debut against Greece in 2024 Credit: AFP

A two-time Premier League champion, Jones featured 49 times for Liverpool in all competitions last season.

But the incident with Szboszlai has not reflected well on the former European U-21 champion.

Peterborough owner and Liverpool fan Darragh MacAnthony blasted Jones on talkSPORT, saying on Thursday: "He's acting like a spoilt brat.

"I saw his behaviour last night on the pitch... I understand the frustration that he should have got the armband. He's a Scouser; he's been there 20 years, blah blah blah.

"But to act like that and to carry it on, because it went on for about two minutes.

"He was having a go at Szoboszlai, who handed the armband over, I think, to Tsimikas, I believe Curtis Jones had the temper tantrum over that.

"That behaviour can't happen, not from a graduate from the academy; he's too into himself."

Sports.title: Liverpool's second-half changes exposed Andoni Iraola's blunt attack but the new boss MUST give starts to two teenagers - while Daniel Farke faces a huge call as Leeds aim to make a big push
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola was left with plenty to ponder as he jetted back across the Atlantic after his Liverpool side blew a two-goal lead to be well beaten by Leeds in Chicago.

In the Reds’ final game of this pre-season tour, early goals from young defender Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz had Liverpool on their way to a perfect trip but, after both teams made half-time changes, Leeds vastly improved to triumph.

At the home of NFL side Chicago Bears, two American football-style throw-ins undid Liverpool as Dominic Calvert-Lewin scored a brace. Joe Rodon and Sean Longstaff also bagged for Daniel Farke’s side as Leeds bombarded the penalty area with set-pieces.

Liverpool throw it away

This was a game worthy of the dictionary definition for the old ‘game of two halves’ cliche.

When Wirtz, Isak, Ngumoha and Nyoni went off, Liverpool had nothing going forward. Likewise, the half-time introductions of Calvert-Lewin, Wilson et al gave Leeds the spark that was missing.

But it was two Hail Mary-style throw-ins that propelled Leeds to victory. Shrewd runs off the ball from Calvert-Lewin, abysmal defending from Liverpool. Given the Reds’ set-piece frailties last season, it is a glaringly obvious area to improve.

Liverpool threw away a 2-0 lead against Leeds in their final match of their pre-season tour

Florian Wirtz ha scored a fine goal but the Reds had no attacking threat when he and others went off

It does not help that several senior defenders are injured, with Jeremie Frimpong limping off in the second half. The Dutchman’s issue is the fifth in the back four with Joe Gomez, Conor Bradley, Jeremy Jacquet and Giovanni Leoni all out – and captain Virgil van Dijk not on this trip.

Two teenagers push for starts

Rio Ngumoha is so talented that, in the eyes of many, he is not counted as one of the kids looking to break through any more.

It is easy to forget he is still just 17. This time last year, he was yet to make his Premier League debut.

Now, it would be a surprise if Ngumoha, capped by England in a pre-World Cup friendly, did not start the first game of the upcoming season.

Liverpool are trying to sign Paris Saint-Germain’s Bradley Barcola but that should not halt Ngumoha’s meteoric rise.

The winger is ready for the next step, which is playing more often after five league starts last term. He terrorised wing back James Justin here.

The breakout star of this tour, though, has been another teenager: Trey Nyoni. The 19-year-old made six substitute appearances in the league last term but is ready for more.

Midfielder Nyoni has bossed players ten years his senior on this tour, dictating play from deep. He is small in stature but can be a giant for Iraola in the coming years.

With Alexis Mac Allister still absent after making the World Cup final with Argentina, Ryan Gravenberch only just back and Curtis Jones the subject of interest in a move away, is Nyoni’s time now?

Still just 17, it would be a surprise if Rio Ngumoha did not start Liverpool's season opener

It could be Trey Nyoni's time, meanwhile, with the 19-year-old shining while on tour

Should Farke stick or twist with the winning formula?

Farke was sleep-walking towards the sack as Christmas approached last year, with Leeds in the relegation zone with a run of six defeats in the seven games.

But the boss changed formation to a back five and, from December 1 onwards, Leeds only lost six of 25 matches and got to an FA Cup semi-final.

Farke is not a negative coach by nature and the stubborn system may be unnatural but the signs are that he is set to stick by it.

The verdict here in Illinois? In the first half, it was worrying: they looked vulnerable at the back and created very little on the counter-attack.

After the break and a quadruple change – but the same system – they looked in fine fettle and played Liverpool off the park. The exercise will prompt both managers to know their best XIs.

Leeds could make a push – with a few more signings

Leeds were ten times better after the break.

With James Trafford expected to become their record signing for around £45million, this could be a window that gives Leeds a platform for a top-half push, especially after tempting Wilson to join on a free transfer from Fulham.

However, they are still light in some positions. Gabriel Gudmundsson limping off in the first half highlighted left back as a problem area, while the forward line could do with being strengthened after missing out on Julian Brandt and seeing Jack Harrison depart.

New £34million defender Tarik Muharemovic looks a solid buy from Sassuolo to replace Pascal Struijk.

Leeds could push for a top-half finish if they pick up a few more summer signings

Wirtz in full Flo already

Wirtz and Alexander Isak both struggled to live up to hopes or expectations last season due to fitness and form issues.

Arne Slot had many issues but the Dutchman might have had better success if he had been able to call upon a fully fit-and-firing version of the duo, who cost £241million combined.

Both are back with a point to prove now, though – and new boss Iraola knows he too will be unable to achieve his ambitions without these two on song.

On their first pre-season outings after a post-World Cup break, both looked sharp. Wirtz took his goal nicely and also played some gasp-inducing passes, while Isak seemed to be full of confidence. The second-half fall-off shows their importance.

Sports.title: Furious UEFA warned Gianni Infantino NOT to destroy botched World Cup plan documents with lawsuit threatened before FIFA president abandoned his plot
Sports.content:
Furious UEFA warned Gianni Infantino NOT to destroy botched World Cup plan documents with lawsuit threatened before FIFA president abandoned his plot

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

UEFA reportedly threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action over his botched plan to sell off the World Cup to private investors.

The FIFA president was forced to abandon a hugely controversial proposal to sell stakes in the tournament to a group led by Josh Kushner, the brother of Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared, on Saturday, following a major revolt from the footballing world.

That heaped the pressure on Infantino, with UEFA subsequently declaring a loss of confidence in the Italian-Swiss administrator.

European football's governing body had previously led the rebellion, announcing on Thursday that their 55 member nations would boycott the World Cup if the plans weren't scrapped.

And now, according to The Telegraph, UEFA threatened to go to court over the scheme, which was known as FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), in a letter they sent to Infantino on Friday.

The report adds that UEFA also wrote to Kushner, Greg Maffei, JPMorgan and OpenEconomics, and said they were 'actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints' as a result of the collapsed proposal.

UEFA reportedly threatened Gianni Infantino with legal action over his botched World Cup plan

FIFA president Infantino pictured with his UEFA counterpart Aleksander Ceferin in 2024

As reported in The Telegraph, the letter to Infantino read: 'Uefa hereby gives formal notice that it is actively considering legal action, arbitration, and/or regulatory complaints (together, the “proceedings”) arising out of and in connection with the FFE plan proposed by Fifa and all related matters as further described below.

'You and Fifa are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this notice that are in your or Fifa’s possession, custody, or control.'

UEFA went on to warn FIFA that 'any destruction, deletion, alteration, concealment or loss of relevant materials' after their letter 'may constitute spoliation of evidence'.

They then refused to rule out further action if any of the aforementioned actions took place.

The letter also insisted that FIFA must ensure that certain individuals, including Infantino, Arsene Wenger, FIFA's chief of global football development, secretary general Mattias Grafstrom and Kevin Lamour, FIFA's chief operating officer, 'specifically preserve all such materials in their possession'.

Kushner was expected to lead the proposed investor group through his Thrive Eternal fund, while Maffei, who is a Trump donor, was also set to be involved.

JPMorgan and OpenEconomics were reported as being involved in the search for investors.

UEFA also wrote to Joshua Kushner, who was expected to lead the group of private investors

Speaking on Saturday as he announced the abandonment of his plans, Infantino said: 'The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed.

'And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.

'Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.'

He continued: 'Our purpose has always been - and will always be - to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.

'Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, and particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.'

The statement marked an embarrassing u-turn for Infantino, given it came less than 24 hours after he attempted to clarify his plans and blamed the media for misconstruing them.

It remains to be seen what happens to the FIFA president, with Infantino having previously been expected to run unopposed in the governing body's elections next March.

That may change now, while FIFA member nations could trigger a vote of no confidence to oust Infantino. The threshold to initiate the process is 46 FIFA member associations. For context, UEFA have 55 members.

Sports.title: Argentinian star signs for Chelsea, Newcastle's £27m goalkeeping target completes medical, Bournemouth bag Sevilla ace - while Hull are set to beat Rangers and Cardiff City to highly-rated Norwegian: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Blues sign England nemesis

Chelsea have completed the signing of Argentina midfielder Valentin Barco from sister club Strasbourg on a seven-year contract.

The 22-year-old stirred controversy when his over-zealous celebrations of Argentina's victory over England at the World Cup provoked an angry reaction from Jude Bellingham.

Barco, who previously made six Premier League appearances for Brighton, has been signed following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid earlier this summer but he has been playing in midfield.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in May, he left for Chelsea at the end of the season, saying his farewells to Strasbourg supporters.

Chelsea are also continuing negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Chelsea have completed the signing of England World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco (right)

Tractor Boys close in on new midfielder

Ipswich Town are closing in on the £16million signing of Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

As Daily Mail Sport reported last week, the Portuguese midfielder was leaning towards a move to Portman Road after they declared their interest even though Hull City had been in advanced talks over an initial loan for the 26-year-old.

However, Hull City boss Sergej Jakirovic revealed over the weekend that they were set to miss out to a club that was willing to sign him on a permanent deal.

Spurs target Liverpool star

Tottenham have made their interest known in Cody Gakpo but Liverpool have no plans to sell.

Liverpool, who continue to work on a deal for Paris Saint-Germain's Bradley Barcola, are looking to add attacking quality rather than lose it. Gakpo, 27, is one year in to a new long-term contract and with current market prices escalating for players of his experience, it would take a huge sum to change Liverpool's stance.

Tottenham are also keeping a watching brief on Omar Marmoush at Manchester City as well as negotiating for Savinho.

Newcastle's new No 1 completes medical ahead of transfer

Goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek has completed his Newcastle United medical in Spain, and is set to be announced as the club’s latest signing.

Newcastle activated his £25.7m release clause and the player travelled to La Manga on Saturday.

As Daily Mail Sport revealed, the 24-year-old Czech is being brought in as the club’s new first-choice option in goal.

Lukas Hornicek has completed his medical ahead of joining Newcastle in a £25.7million deal

Bournemouth bolster full-back options

Bournemouth have agreed an £11.2m deal with Sevilla for right-back Juanlu Sanchez.

The deal is worth £9.5m plus a potential £1.7m in add-ons while Sevilla retain a 10 per sell-on.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Saturday, Bournemouth accelerated talks as they needed a right-back after the departure of Alex Jimenez to Fiorentina.

The 22-year-old Juanlu is a Spain international with four caps and had interest from Everton.

Wigan chasing Chelsea starlet

Chelsea midfielder Reggie Walsh is wanted on loan at Wigan Athletic.

The two clubs recently did business together when Chelsea completed the transfer of highly-rated 19-year-old midfielder Harrison Bettoni from Wigan on a four year contract.

Walsh became Chelsea’s youngest player to feature in the Champions League last season and will be hoping to build on his senior breakthrough during the 2026-27 campaign.

He figured briefly in the friendly defeat to Spurs in the Sydney Cup and was among several academy players involved as Xabi Alonso took charge of his first training session, alongside senior players such as Cole Palmer and João Pedro.

Walsh has returned to pre-season looking physically bigger and stronger so Chelsea are keen to see how he copes with more competitive game time.

Hammers chase former Spurs star

West Ham have joined the clubs showing interest in AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott.

Como, Ajax, PSV Eindhoven and Real Betis have already made enquiries.

The former Tottenham academy graduate is in demand after scoring 31 goals last season.

Alkmaar though are reluctant to sell the 24-year-old Republic of Ireland international to a rival Dutch club.

West Ham have entered the race to sign former Tottenham forward Troy Parrott

Hull lead race for Norwegian star

Hull City are ready to fend off interest from Rangers and Cardiff City to sign highly-rated Norwegian midfielder Jens Hjerto-Dahl.

Cardiff had offered a club record fee for the 20-year-old from Tromso but Hull are offering him the chance to play in the Premier League.

The 6ft 4ins defensive midfielder has captained Norway at youth level and is an U21 international.

Hull are also advancing in talks for 18-year-old centre back Lucas Herrington from Colorado Rapids and winger Mohamed-Ali Cho from Nice.

Moore to go on loan

Cologne have asked to take Tottenham winger Mikey Moore on loan.

The 18-year-old has a number of options including an offer to return on loan to Rangers.

In the air tonight

Mathew Collins, the son of music star Phil Collins, has signed for German side 1860 Munich after impressing during a trial.

The 21-year-old midfielder has signed a contract until 2027 after joining the club's first-team squad for pre-season, where he convinced the coaching staff with his performances in training and friendly matches.

'Mathew has made a very good impression on us,' 1860 managing director Thomas Probst said. 'He integrated into the team very quickly and is an asset to us both on and off the pitch.'

WEDNESDAY: Man City push for World Cup wonderkid amid doubts over Rodri's future

Sports.title: 'Gutted' former Premier League star Charlie Austin reveals he has been rejected from first coaching job by former club QPR
Sports.content:
'Gutted' former Premier League star Charlie Austin reveals he has been rejected from first coaching job by former club QPR

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Former Premier League forward Charlie Austin has revealed he has been rejected from his first coaching role by former club Queens Park Rangers.

Austin, 37, has hung up his boots from playing professionally after a career spanning 20 years, and is now trying to continue his time in the game by helping bring through the next generation.

He revealed on Sunday that he had tried for a job at former club QPR, where he enjoyed three separate spells as a player, but came up short.

The forward wrote on social media: 'First job interview disappointment. Gutted not to progress to the next stage for @QPRAcademy coaching team. The club I really wanted to work with.

'Will keep working hard and hoping my time will come. Good luck to whoever lands the role, what a club you get to join!'

Austin played 148 times for QPR, scoring 61 goals. He featured for the club between 2013 and 2016, 2021 on loan, then again permanently between 2021 and 2022.

Charlie Austin has expressed his disappointment at being turned down for a coaching job at former side QPR

He also featured for the likes of Southampton, Burnley and West Brom in his playing career.

One fan asked him in response to his post whether he expected to get the job at QPR due to his past with the club.

Austin replied: 'No hidden agenda. Just honest disappointment at missing out on a role at a club I think highly of.

'Nothing but respect for QPR, the process was fair and professional, everyone was great.

'As I said will keep working hard for my time to come! This just weren't my time.'

Other fans didn't shy away from giving their thoughts, either.

One wrote in reply: 'I feel that the reason you have posted this is to get a reaction due to you previously playing for them. Welcome to the real world, maybe you just didn’t interview well enough. Brush up on those interview skills I say.'

Some, though, were more sympathetic.

One posted: 'How on earth could they reject you? That is diabolical.'

Comedian Seann Walsh, who is a QPR fan, added: 'You’ll be back, mate. Destiny x.'

Austin is currently playing for semi-professional club Hungerford Town, who play in the Southern League Division One South.

Sports.title: Robert Lewandowski makes perfect start to MLS life with Chicago Fire as city lands the star attraction they have so desperately craved after missing out on Neymar, writes LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Chicago prides itself on being one of the sporting capitals of the world.

It was the setting for the legendary era of Michael Jordan, Scottie Pippen and Dennis Rodman as part of the Chicago Bulls’ six NBA titles in the 1990s, as seen in The Last Dance docu-series on Netflix which many watched in the Covid-19 pandemic.

There is the Bears NFL team and, across the city, Wrigley Field is one of Major League Baseball’s most iconic stadiums and home to the Cubs, city rivals of the White Sox. The ice hockey team, the Blackhawks, often get big crowds.

Lagging somewhat behind, although certainly on the rise now, is the local football team. Fandom for Chicago Fire is spreading across the city at a rate not too much slower than the great fire of 1871 from which the team – and the hit US television show – takes its name.

The reason? One of the greatest strikers of his generation in Robert Lewandowski, with a helping hand from a lesser-known Englishman pulling the strings.

Daily Mail Sport was in situ at Soldier Field as the big Polishman opened his account for his new team, signing on the back of winning 10 German Bundesligas (two with Borussia Dortmund, eight with Bayern Munich), a Champions League and three La Liga titles with Barcelona.

A home debut brace and the game-winner ✌️🔥



Robert Lewandowski's first match in Chicago is one to remember. pic.twitter.com/pt567KCnn0 — Major League Soccer (@MLS) August 2, 2026

Robert Lewandowski scored twice for Chicago Fire on his home MLS debut following his summer move from Barcelona

The man who brought him to Major League Soccer (MLS) is a 50-year-old born in Bedford, who has also held jobs as academy manager for Luton, Norwich and one of Europe’s success stories in Norwegian side Bodo/Glimt, who beat Manchester City, Atletico Madrid and Inter this year.

Gregg Broughton, who joined as sporting director after doing the same role at Blackburn, tells Daily Mail Sport on Lewandowski: ‘Robert had been somebody the club had their eyes on for a long time. We understand how MLS works. There is a huge Polish community here in Chicago.

‘We tried to sign Neymar in January 2025, we could not get that done but he shared an agent with Lewandowski. We knew he would have his pick of clubs in Europe, in Saudi Arabia and he might have done another year at Barca. We had to make Chicago Fire his choice.

‘So our head coach Gregg Berhalter (formerly of the US national team) went to Barcelona, Robert’s wife came here for a business trip so we took her out. We sent a private jet to Barca to pick him and his representatives up, bring them here and show them the city.

‘He knows what world-class looks like, he is alongside Messi and Ronaldo, he is perfect for us. Robert is humble, easy to get on with, drives standards every day, won’t accept things being anything except everyone giving their best at every moment.’

Lewandowski’s record speaks for itself: 41 goals in 82 Lech Poznan games, 103 in 187 for Dortmund, 344 in 375 for Bayern, 120 in 193 for Barca. In 2020, he scored 55 in 47, won the Champions League and was arguably robbed of a Ballon d’Or, it being canned due to Covid.

He scored twice on his home debut on Saturday as Fire beat Charlotte FC 2-1, a team managed by ex-Aston Villa, Brentford and Leicester boss Dean Smith with several other Englishmen including midfielder Ashley Westwood, once of Villa, Burnley and Crewe Alexandra.

The 37-year-old is clearly the star attraction. Just as sport atheists would flock to watch Jordan in the 1990s, there are Lewandowski shirts across the city and a huge influx of Polish fans at Soldier Field stadium, which made for a raucous atmosphere not associated with MLS.

The forward is a mega star and the United States side worked hard to bring him to the club

‘I’m really happy to be here,’ said Lewandowski. ‘I enjoy every day: the lifestyle, the club and the organisation. Everything is really at a top level. I cannot say one bad word about the club, and I’m very impressed that everything is working very well, both on and off the pitch.’

The state-of-the-art facilities are part of the sales pitch to future transfer targets and a big reason why Chicago Fire allow teams to train at their base – Manchester United and Liverpool have done so, while Germany recently used it as their World Cup camp.

Those at the club believe seeing their base can plant a seed of thought in players’ minds ahead of a future move to MLS. Club staffers joked to Daily Mail Sport this week that it was a shame Virgil van Dijk is not on this pre-season tour for Liverpool, given his deal is up next summer.

‘Chicago is an incredible city,’ adds Broughton. ‘The training ground is incredible and that is allowing us to build a world-class club, we are building a new stadium. American sport accepts you can take five years to rebuild a squad, in Europe you don’t have that time.

‘I want to achieve on-field success and the bigger picture is I want to build upon the footprint of the World Cup and Club World Cup here in America. Twenty years ago, you never saw football shirts here – now, down by the river, they’re everywhere.

‘But we want them to be Chicago Fire shirts. This city stops to talk about sport. When the Bears got to the play-offs, the queues just to get into bars were crazy, you can’t get a ticket for love nor money. We know football can do that and the plan is to get Fire to be part of that.’

Lewandowski can certainly help.

Sports.title: Glasgow has shown the Commonwealth Games are worth fighting for - now they MUST come back on free-to-air TV, writes NIK SIMON
Sports.content:
Glasgow has shown the Commonwealth Games are worth fighting for - now they MUST come back on free-to-air TV, writes NIK SIMON

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Anyone who claims the Commonwealth Games mean nothing should speak to the crowd that gathered outside my hotel at 1am on Friday.

‘Let’s go to Maccies!’ bellowed a late-night reveller. I looked out the window and it was Emily Campbell, hours after winning gold in the weightlifting, leading a group of athletes and supporters on a night out in Glasgow.

One of the best things about these games, not by design, is how close the locals have been able to get to the competitors. One cost-cutting decision was to sacrifice the athletes’ village, meaning competitors have been scattered in hotels across the city.

It has been impossible to miss the tracksuits of 74 different nations that have descended upon Scotland for the past 11 days of competition. The fans have never felt closer.

Josh Kerr went for a jog along the river before winning gold in the mile. Duncan Scott fuelled up for the pool with a hefty breakfast at a cafe on Wilson Street. Even Adam Ramsay-Peaty had to catch the bus.

One downside of these games has been the lack of visibility to the casual sports fan. For the first time in 72 years, the BBC pulled out as the official broadcaster. TNT Sports has provided comprehensive coverage but the events have not cut through to the UK’s mainstream audience.

The Glasgow Commonwealth Games have been a huge success over the past week-and-a-half

The absence of household names like Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson is a blow though

Given the absence of household names such as Olympic champion Keely Hodgkinson, this competition does not have the clout to pull in subscribers. Joe Public will not go out of his way to find the bowls or an obscure judo bout.

How many people would have tuned in to watch Matt Weston win his Winter Olympics gold medals in Italy, if the skeleton had not been broadcast live on the BBC? Not many.

These Games have been packed with feel-good stories. They have offered the perfect antidote to the grubby boardroom battles at FIFA HQ, where Gianni Infantino has been trying to make a quick buck from selling the World Cup to the highest bidder.

With more exposure, the likes of Cyrille Tchatchet would have been front of the queue to sit on the One Show sofa this week. He overcame homelessness to win weightlifting silver for England, but will now return to the gym to train in relative obscurity.

This event is ripe for free-to-air TV — particularly if most of the superstars stay away — and a new UK broadcast arrangement must be top of the agenda for the 2030 edition in India.

‘The BBC has been a fantastic partner for a very long period, and we do have a relationship with them for this games,’ said Katie Sadleir, chief executive officer of the Commonwealth Games Federation. ‘We are doing BBC Radio, so they are involved.

‘We are thrilled with TNT and Warner Bros. Discovery [TNT’s parent company]. For £4.99 for 600 hours compared to 200 hours in Birmingham [who hosted the Games in 2022], we are very pleased with that relationship.

‘We are moving towards a much wider feel about how people consume the games. I look after the Commonwealth movement of 74 countries, and it is my responsibility to look globally in terms of viewership.

‘It’s a process we will work through with the organising committee in terms of who the broadcaster is for 2030. The BBC will definitely be part of that mix.’

This event was almost abandoned when Victoria pulled out as hosts three years ago.

Australia’s richest person, mining magnate Gina Rinehart, has been offering cash bonuses for her country’s podium finishers, ensuring they arrived with a packed squad and walked away on top of the medal count. Channel 7’s coverage reached 11.39 million in Down Under. Australia’s credibility will be damaged if they bid for future sporting events. Perhaps Rinehart should have stepped in sooner?

But Glasgow saved the day. Yes, there have been some empty seats, but the big-ticket events have sold out. They have not spent taxpayer money and their fit-for-purpose model could provide a blueprint for hosting events during days of economic uncertainty.

The athletes are closer to stars than ever before and there has been a buzz around the city (pictured - Scotland's Josh after winning the Men's One Mile final)

After uncertainty about the event, Glasgow saved the day and proved to be brilliant hosts

India have promised to supersize things for Ahmedabad 2030. They hope to sell out the world’s largest stadium and use the event to showcase their credentials as Olympic hosts.

Proposals have been made to turn the Commonwealths into a qualifying event for World Championships. But unless the Games can lure back all of the biggest names of track and field, the Glasgow model — backed up by terrestrial TV — may well be the future.

For now, it looks more like a launchpad for young Olympic hopefuls. Filip Nowacki and Amalie Smith have emerged as Team GB prospects in the pool, Henry Hobbs won gold on the bike and Emily Newnham showed promise on the track.

‘It’s an incredible opportunity for a lot of athletes,’ said Ramsay-Peaty. ‘It is a stepping stone to give a platform two years out from an Olympics. That’s why we have got to nurture it.’

The games have been reset and reimagined. The Glaswegian hosts have cut their cloth and done so with a smile.

‘People are talking about these Games on the streets,’ added Sadleir. ‘Everyone is going away buzzed about what happened and what they think the future is for the Commonwealth Sport movement.’

Sports.title: Boxer in 'critical but stable' condition after being rushed to hospital following sickening knockout as promoter Frank Warren issues statement
Sports.content:
Boxer in 'critical but stable' condition after being rushed to hospital following sickening knockout as promoter Frank Warren issues statement

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Boxer Lee Reeves is 'critical but stable' having been hospitalised after being knocked out during his defeat by Gary Cully on Saturday night.

In what proved to be an enthralling all-Republic of Ireland bout, Reeves was stopped in the 10th and final round by Cully - who sent him tumbling to the canvas with a huge left hand.

There was immediate concern from those inside the 3Arena in Dublin as Reeves stayed down for several moments as officials and medical staff quickly came to his aid.

The 31-year-old was given some oxygen before he left the venue being carried off on a stretcher and taken to hospital.

A spokesperson from Queensberry Promotions said on Sunday evening: 'Lee Reeves is still in hospital, in a critical but stable condition.

'We will know more in the coming days, and our thoughts and prayers remain with Lee and his family.'

Lee Reeves (right) was rushed to hospital after being knocked out by Gary Cully on Saturday

Reeves was immeadiately attended to by after being stopped in the 10th round of his defeat - he is now 'stable but critical'

Taking to X to provide an update, Queensberry promoter Frank Warren had previously written: 'All our thoughts and prayers are with Lee Reeves and his family at this time as he remains in hospital.

'Everyone at Queensberry is thinking of him and we're in constant contact with his team regarding his condition as we hope for positive news.'

Victory for Cully meant he claimed the BUI Celtic super-lightweight title but despite the victory, his thoughts were with Reeves.

'My prayers and thoughts are with Lee Reeves, hopefully he's okay,' said a concerned Cully.

'He came in there as a big underdog after fighting relatively at a lower level up until now, but he really showed that he can operate at a higher level. Huge credit to him.'

Sports.title: England's World Cup nemesis Valentin Barco joins Chelsea: Argentina star who provoked Three Lions in semi-final defeat confirms switch to Stamford Bridge after Atlanta antics
Sports.content:
Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal.

Barco, 22, who can play in midfield and at left-back, joins the Blues from their sister club Strasbourg.

The Argentine hit the headlines last month when he clashed with Jude Bellingham after England's semi-final defeat at the World Cup.

Barco made just one substitute appearance at the tournament, but he infuriated the Three Lions after he sprinted across the pitch when Enzo Fernandez equalised late on in the clash.

He ran right in front of several England players and appeared to taunt them, before John Stones reacted by giving him a shove.

Barco later also came onto the pitch in the aftermath of Lautaro Martinez's winning goal.

Chelsea have confirmed the signing of World Cup villain Valentin Barco on a seven-year deal

Barco clashed with Jude Bellingham after Argentina's semi-final victory over England

There were also reports that the new Chelsea star had been winding up the England bench for the entirety of the 90 minutes.

In response to his antics, Bellingham gave the 22-year-old a slap on the back of the head after the full-time whistle as Argentina's players celebrated, causing a scuffle on the pitch.

Given his involvement in the World Cup, Barco won't join up with his new team-mates until later in pre-season.

The versatile star began his career back home with Boca Juniors, making his debut at the age of 16.

After impressing in Argentina, Barco joined Brighton in 2024 for £7.4million yet he struggled to establish himself on the south coast, and spent time on loan at Sevilla and Strasbourg.

He joined Strasbourg permanently in July 2025 and was regularly linked with a move away after impressing in France, where his side qualified for Europe.

Barco contributed 12 goals and assists last season and his strong form saw him earn a place in Argentina's World Cup squad, although he played just 19 minutes in a group stage victory over Jordan.

Bellingham slapped Barco on the back of the head following his overzealous celebrations

His arrival at Stamford Bridge comes following the exit of Marc Cucurella to Real Madrid, although Chelsea are still in negotiations with Rayo Vallecano for left wing-back Pep Chavarria after making an improved offer.

Barco is the Blues' seventh signing of the summer, with Danny Welbeck, Morgan Rogers, Maxence Lacroix, Geovany Quenda, Marco Palestra and former Strasbourg striker Emmanuel Emegha all also joining the club.

He has similarly become the 13th player to move between the French side and Chelsea since BlueCo took over Strasbourg in 2023, a year after they purchased the Premier League side.

Sports.title: Preston vs Barcelona friendly cancelled hours before kick-off for bizarre reason
Sports.content:
Preston vs Barcelona friendly cancelled hours before kick-off for bizarre reason

Preston North End's pre-season friendly with Barcelona has been cancelled at the 11th hour, with the Championship side set to face the Spanish giants in a behind-closed-doors match at St. George's Park

View 2 Images Barcelona are in the United Kingdom for pre-season (Image: James Gill - Danehouse, Getty Images)

Barcelona's pre-season friendly against Prest North End has been called off just one day before it was meant to take place. The La Liga giants were scheduled to face the Championship side in a behind-closed-doors friendly at St. George's Park.

‌



Hansi Flick's side are currently in the United Kingdom preparing for the new season, and played Birmingham City last week, losing the match on penalties. The hope of being able to get another intense runout in for Karim Adeyemi and co, while much of the squad is yet to return from their break following the World Cup, failed to come to fruition, however.

‌



Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo reports that Preston were unwilling to risk more senior stars for the match and instead proposed a game with their under-21 squad, being unable to fill the places for a full senior squad. The suggestion was declined by Barca, who have decided to hold a normal training session in its place.

‌



Preston take on Huddersfield Town in the League Cup in the coming days and were not willing to risk further injuries as a result. Barcelona will soon return to Spain, earlier than planned, to continue their preparations.

They will take on British opposition, with two further pre-season matches lined up against Udinese and Nottingham Forest next weekend. Flick's side will travel to Italy to play in the three-team tournament, with three 45-minute matches taking place at the Bluenergy Stadium in Udine.

Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend READ MORE :

5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job READ MORE :

Following that, they will take on Egyptian outfit Al Ahly in the prestigious Joan Gamper Trophy at Camp Nou, serving as the final preparation before the campaign begins.

‌



By contrast, Preston had taken on Stockport County over the weekend before their season kicks off. Off the pitch, the Lancashire club have been left reeling following alleged attempts by Wrexham to secure captain Ben Whiteman.

A transfer worth around £2million has been suggested, with boss Paul Heckingbottom delivering a stark verdict on the situation. Speaking to BBC Radio Lancashire, Heckingbottom said: "Ben told me, told Peter (Ridsdale, CEO) he's played his last game for the club. He's trying to force a move, which is an issue for me, for the players."

View 2 Images St. George's Park was set to host the friendly (Image: Getty)

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"We've been in regular conversations in the last few days, and Ben knew there was a line I didn't want him to cross," Heckingbottom added. "Unfortunately, he has, and you can't have that.

"My priority now is the players that are here and the players who want to play for us, and represent the club... Listen, there's a valuation on him. I just hope for Ben's sake that Wrexham are willing to pay it, otherwise he's put himself in a really sticky situation."

Article continues below

The League Cup has already got underway with Rochdale knocking out Tranmere on penalties in a preliminary round. York welcome Crawley Town in the only other preliminary match on Monday.

Sports.title: Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Monday’s three meetings, including Nottingham Nap
Sports.content:
Newsboy’s horseracing tips for Monday’s three meetings, including Nottingham Nap

Newsboy fancies his Nap, Theme Park, to thrill at Nottingham and also hopes Leucothea can score on the same card and complete his Daily Double

View 2 Images Nottingham hosts a six-race Flat meeting on Monday when Newsboy’s nap, Theme Park, is fancied to win the finale (5.10) (Image: Getty Images)

ENJOY the ride with THEME PARK (5.10, Nap) in the concluding Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap at Nottingham on Monday. After a fruitless 2025, the Nigel Tinkler-trained six-year-old made it third time lucky this season with a length-and-a-quarter victory from Chilly Breeze in a one-mile handicap at Doncaster on July 23. Sports.title: Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend
Sports.content:
Man Utd transfer imminent as Michael Carrick greenlights rapid deal this weekend

Manchester United goalkeeper Altay Bayindir is set to leave Old Trafford this summer, with the Turkey international expected to join La Liga side Celta Vigo on a loan deal

View 2 Images Michael Carrick faces a busy summer as Manchester United manager (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Altay Bayindir is getting closer to completing a move away from Manchester United this summer. La Liga club Celta Vigo are set to sign the Turkey international.

‌



United signed Bayindir from Fenerbahce in the summer of 2023, but the shot-stopper has made just 17 appearances during his three years at Old Trafford. Bayindir joined United to serve as the understudy to Andre Onana, which was the case for his first two years at the club.

‌



That changed last summer when Senne Lammens signed for the Red Devils and went on to become the club’s new No.1 goalkeeper. Bayindir's prospects at United have been shrouded in doubt for quite some time, particularly following the club's decision to bring in Karl Darlow on a free transfer earlier this summer.

‌



Man Utd star claims club can win Premier League after mood change under Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

It has now been reported by Metropolitano that Celta Vigo are on the brink of signing Bayindir on a loan basis from United, with the deal said to be almost entirely wrapped up in quick fashion. The same report suggests that the La Liga club are hopeful of formally announcing the agreement to sign Bayindir next week, with the goalkeeper anticipated to join his new squad at a training camp in Italy.

A separate report from Spanish publication AS claims that the 28-year-old is expected to undergo a medical to complete his move to Celta Vigo on either Sunday or Monday. Our sister title The Manchester Evening News reported on Saturday that Celta Vigo are leading the chase to secure Bayindir's signature, with the goalkeeper appearing increasingly likely to depart the club in the coming days.

View 2 Images Altay Bayindir looks to be on his way out of Old Trafford (Image: FIFA via Getty Images)

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Despite the mounting interest in Bayindir, United still included the Turkey international in their squad for Saturday night's pre-season friendly against Atletico Madrid in Sweden. Bryan Mbeumo netted twice as United secured a 2-1 triumph over the Spanish side in Stockholm on Saturday evening.

Speaking after the win, Carrick told MUTV: “The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Article continues below

It remains unclear precisely when Bayindir's United departure could be announced, though all indications suggest the goalkeeper's stint at the club is drawing to a close, albeit via a loan arrangement.

Sports.title: 5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job
Sports.content:
5 contenders to replace Gianni Infantino as embattled FIFA chief fights to save job

Gianni Infantino's job security as FIFA president has taken a huge blow following the major backlash towards his controversial plans - and efforts are being made to oust him

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is reportedly reluctant to challenge Gianni Infantino

Gianni Infantino's days as FIFA president appear to be numbered after his plans to sell stakes in tournaments to investors backfired spectacularly.

‌



Infantino clearly misjudged the reaction to his secretive plot and could pay for the mistake with his job. UEFA, CONCACAF and the Asian Football Confederation all voiced their displeasure with the plans, forcing Infantino to perform a humiliating U-turn.

‌



But his opponents are not satisfied with having killed the plot; they want Infantino gone following 10 years at the top of world football. UEFA are said to be 'accelerating' plans to remove the Swiss and FIFA insiders believe he is now 'certain' to go.

‌



If Infantino doesn't resign, then his opponents may have to force a vote of no confidence in his leadership, or back a rival in the upcoming FIFA presidential election. So who could put their name forward by November 18 to succeed Infantino in the election next year?

As the chiefs of world football scheme away behind the scenes, Mirror Football takes a look at five possible contenders.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Gianni Infantino sent overwhelming FIFA quit verdict as 99% call for him to go READ MORE :

Victor Montagliani

The Canadian is the CONCACAF president and has emerged as one of the main contenders in a chaotic past few days. CONCACAF rejected FIFA's proposal for private investment, but was less critical in its words than UEFA.

Montagliani is a long-time ally of Infantino's but is reportedly ready to stand against him in the elections. Before the scandal, the 60-year-old was not going to challenge Infantino - who had been set to run unopposed - but had an eye on going for the role in 2031.

Yet Infantino's sudden unpopularity has seen Montagliani sense an opportunity with his involvement in the World Cup boosting his profile and credentials. He was the first non-Caribbean CONCACAF president since 1969 when he took over and is said to have support beyond his own federation.

‌



View 4 Images CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani is one of the contenders (Image: Elizabeth Ruiz Ruiz/Getty Images)

Nasser al-Khelaifi

The Paris Saint-Germain president is one of the most powerful figures in football. The Qatari leads the European Football Clubs umbrella group and is extremely influential in European club football.

Al-Khelaifi has plenty of allies and has been suggested as the next FIFA president. The only problem is that he is reportedly not keen, with a source saying he has "absolutely no ambition, no intention, nor any interest in this role at FIFA".

‌



The chances of him changing his mind now appear even less likely after the Qatar Football Association put out a statement backing Infantino on Sunday.

View 4 Images Nasser al-Khelaifi is a powerful figure in European football (Image: LOU BENOIST/AFP via Getty Images)

Mattias Granstrom

Granstrom is the FIFA general secretary and is seen as the most likely internal candidate to step up and replace Infantino. While he lacks the profile of the other candidates, he has reportedly not been tarnished by Infantino's plan and could therefore garner support, were he to consider running.

‌



Dariusz Mioduski

The Polish lawyer is currently the vice-president of the European Football Clubs body, as well as president and owner of Legia Warsaw. His name has come up in the swirling rumour mill of the past few days

Mioduski has been backed by the Belgian, Spanish, Norwegian, German and Swedish associations, according to a report from talkSPORT earlier this month. With UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin reportedly unwilling to challenge for the FIFA presidency, Mioduski could become the European candidate.

View 4 Images Dariusz Mioduski has supporters in Europe (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Sheikh Salman bin E brahim Al Khalifa

The Asian Football Confederation (AFC) president is another possible candidate, despite initial reluctance to step forward. The AFC released a statement saying it "stands in solidarity" with UEFA and CONCACAF, but their words were much less fiery and there is reportedly less conviction in the territory's opposition to Infantino's plans.

Al Khalifa is a Bahraini and is very experienced, having been in charge of the AFC since 2013. But it remains to seen whether the 60-year-old wants to put his name forward.

Sports.content:
Man Utd star claims club can win Premier League after mood change under Michael Carrick

Manchester United have not won the Premier League since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, but could finally end the drought in 2026/27

View Image Michael Carrick has his work cut out (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

Leny Yoro believes that Manchester United can win with Premier League this season. That's despite the club's welk-documented struggles for form since Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement 13 years ago.

‌



The legendary Scottish manager earned 13 top-flight titles before bringing the curtain down on a remarkable coaching career in 2013. And in the years since, United have been through seven permanent managers as they have struggled to bring glory back to Old Trafford.

‌



While the club has seen success in various cup competitions in the wake of Fergie's exit, no man has been able to restore Premier League glory. David Moyes scraped a Community Shield in his lacklustre one-year stint with United, while Louis van Gaal saw success in the FA Cup.

‌



Man United icon Casemiro's Inter Miami career off to embarrassing start after nightmare home debut READ MORE :

Man Utd handed £42m transfer blow after Michael Carrick made feelings clear READ MORE :

Jose Mourinho bolstered the Old Trafford silverware collection with a Europa League, an FA Cup and a League Cup across his two-year reign, while Erik ten Hag guided United to both a League Cup and FA Cup triumph during his tenure.

Notably, it was only Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and Ruben Amorim who departed the club empty-handed, leaving behind nothing more than a mixture of fond and forgettable memories from their respective stints in Greater Manchester.

And despite Amorim overseeing a humiliating 15th-place finish in 2024/25, Yoro remains convinced that the tide is turning, with the club setting its sights on ending a 13-year Premier League drought.

‌



When quizzed about the prospect of lifting the Premier League title in the upcoming campaign, he said: "We're Man United so we have to think like that. And I know we have the potential to do it, so we have to do it.
