World.title: The split in Poland’s opposition could help them unseat Tusk’s government [Opinion]
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. By Daniel Tilles If Mateusz Morawiecki cuts his final ties with PiS and forms a new party, it may help broaden the opposition’s appeal by offering voters a more moderate, centre-right option. While the strings have not yet been fully cut, Poland’s main opposition party, the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), is splitting in two. A group of 40 MPs led by former Prime Minister (and PiS deputy leader) Mateusz Morawiecki have now formed a separate parliamentary caucus of their own, after last week refusing to sign a pledge of loyalty and quit the association they had formed – as had been demanded by PiS leader Jarosław Kaczyński. Former Polish PM @MorawieckiM says 41 lawmakers aligned with him will form their own parliamentary caucus, deepening a split in conservative opposition party @pisorgpl. The proposed group would become the third-largest bloc in Poland's Sejmhttps://t.co/coOdpS7pia — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 29, 2026 The move means that Morawiecki’s caucus, known as Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), is now the third largest in parliament, while PiS, which is down to 147 MPs, has lost its status as the biggest. For now, most of Morawiecki’s followers officially remain members of the PiS party, a situation that will only change if they either resign or are thrown out following a disciplinary process that could take weeks. But unless either or both sides make major concessions, it seems only a matter of time before Development Plus becomes a separate party. A lot of international reporting has suggested that these developments will harm Poland’s right-wing opposition and boost the re-election chances of Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s more liberal coalition at next year’s parliamentary elections. In fact, PiS’s split could well help the opposition win a majority. Over the last year, PiS has found itself in an increasingly difficult position. Its support in the polls has fallen below 25%, the party’s lowest level in 14 years. Meanwhile, combined support for two far-right opposition groups – Confederation (Konfederacja) and Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) – has risen to over 20%, threatening PiS’s longstanding dominance on the right. In response, Kaczyński has pushed his party in a more rightward direction, picking a hardline figure, Przemysław Czarnek, as PiS’s prime ministerial candidate in March. That signalled that PiS was aiming to compete head to head with the far right on many issues, taking tougher positions on Ukraine, the EU, migration and climate policy. In many cases, that meant disowning the legacy of the PiS government led by Morawiecki from 2017 to 2023. It also meant that the party was ceding the centre ground, something Morawiecki, who represents the more moderate, technocratic side of PiS, was particularly concerned about (alongside his own waning influence). When in power, PiS launched a revolution in Poland's energy transition. But now, in opposition, it has disowned those achievements and returned to an emphasis on coal. This could be a missed opportunity to win back centrist voters, writes @OrzelBartlomiej https://t.co/8cGvubn7N2 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 29, 2026 Should Morawiecki now, as expected, launch his own centre-right party, focused on economic development, it would appeal to moderate conservatives who are opposed to the Tusk government but put off by the far right and PiS’s own hardline turn. Inevitably, some of the support for Development Plus would come at the expense of PiS – but not all of it, and possibly not even most of it. An example of something similar happening can be seen elsewhere among the opposition. Until last year, KKP was part of Confederation. However, its leader, Grzegorz Braun, was expelled after announcing a run for the presidency against Confederation’s official candidate, Sławomir Mentzen. In June 2025, KKP formed its own parliamentary caucus. Since then, support for Confederation has remained stable at around 13-14%, while KKP has risen to over 9% in the polls. So, by splitting, the two groups actually increased the size of their potential electorate, with KKP successfully appealing to an even more radical pool of voters than Confederation. It is possible that Morawiecki could do the same in the opposite direction – his new party winning over moderate conservatives while PiS continues to appeal to its most loyal supporters as well as competing with the far right. There certainly seems to be fertile ground for such a party. Regular polling by the state research agency CBOS shows that the proportion of Poles with a negative view of Tusk’s government rose to its joint-highest level this month, at 48%, while only 29% have a positive view. The last time that positive views outnumbered negative ones was in February 2024, the second full month of the current ruling coalition’s time in power. Among those who voted for Tusk and his allies in 2023, dissatisfaction is strongest among moderate conservatives. Both Tusk’s centrist KO and one of his coalition partners, The Left (Lewica), are polling only slightly below the proportion of votes they received in that year (30.7% and 8.6%, respectively). However, the most conservative part of the coalition, the centre-right Third Way (Trzecia Droga) alliance, has fallen from 14.4% of the vote in 2023 to only around 4-5% today for the two parties that constituted it, Poland 2050 (Polska 2050) and the Polish People’s Party (PSL) (which last year decided to go their separate ways). An IBRiS poll for Polsat News in April this year found that, whereas 84% of KO voters and 57.1% of Left voters have a positive view of Tusk’s government, that figure falls to 42.5% for Third Way voters, a majority of whom (51.6%) have a negative opinion. PSL and Poland 2050, the two parties that make up the Third Way alliance, have confirmed that they are splitting and will stand separately at the next elections. They will, however, remain part of @donaldtusk's ruling coalition https://t.co/NduEJY25eE — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 18, 2025 Moderate conservatives’ disillusionment with the government, combined with PiS’s shift away from the centre ground, gives a clear opportunity for Morawiecki. And Tusk’s coalition itself showed in 2023 the advantages for the opposition in offering a broader set of options. While some – in KO in particular – had pushed for centrist and left-wing parties to stand jointly on a single list at that year’s elections, instead they campaigned as three main blocs. That gave voters opposed to the PiS government a genuine choice, and likely played a big part in the record turnout that helped bring Tusk’s coalition to power. It is similarly possible now that a four-branched opposition, ranging from Morawiecki on the centre right, through PiS and Confederation, to Braun on the radical right, could together win a parliamentary majority. Polls currently show those four groups with combined support of around 50% (though polling regarding support for Morawiecki’s prospective party should for now be treated with caution). Jestem dumny z tego, co wspólnie zrobiliśmy dla Polski. I wiem jedno – nasza misja wciąż trwa💪🇵🇱#RozwojPlus pic.twitter.com/xOnxKDoroS — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 31, 2026 However, even if they do win a majority, it is far from certain what would happen then. In 2023, the three opposition blocs were, although standing separately, clearly aligned with one another and focused on removing PiS from power. When they together won a parliamentary majority, it was absolutely clear they would form a coalition government. By contrast, today’s opposition is deeply divided. Confederation and KKP regularly attack PiS. It is not at all clear that Confederation would be willing to form a coalition government with PiS, while Kaczyński has explicitly ruled out working with the pro-Russian, anti-American Braun. Meanwhile, Morawiecki’s split has followed months of bitter infighting within PiS, which has often been carried out in public. The manner in which he and his allies are now departing the party means that relations with PiS are likely to remain difficult. The national-conservative opposition PiS party's newly named candidate for prime minister has made overtures to the far-right Confederation. But he also ruled out Grzegorz Braun, an even more radical far-right figure, serving in a PiS-led government https://t.co/i3zOZJWdUN — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 It would therefore be hard for the opposition to form a government, even if they do win a majority. In this situation, the role of President Karol Nawrocki may be vital. Though elected with the support of PiS last year, he was technically an independent and maintained good relations with Confederation and even, to some extent, Braun (who endorsed Nawrocki after being eliminated in the first round). When Morawiecki this week announced the “ten pillars” of Development Plus’s programme, he made clear his loyalty to Nawrocki: the second of those pillars is “respect for the president”. Nie ma silnej Polski bez wielkich ambicji. Nie ma wielkich ambicji bez ludzi, którzy je zdefiniują i będą gotowi wziąć odpowiedzialność za ich realizację. Bezpieczeństwo. Rozwój. Suwerenność. Ambicja. Tożsamość. Patriotyzm. To nie hasła wyborcze, ale fundamenty państwa, które… pic.twitter.com/G0YBbfhLye — Mateusz Morawiecki (@MorawieckiM) July 28, 2026 Many on the right hope that Nawrocki can play a role next year in helping the opposition present a more united front during the election campaign. It is also the president who decides who gets the opportunity to try to form a government after the elections. That role would be of particular significance if, as is very possible, Tusk’s KO emerges as the biggest individual party but the opposition together may be able to form a parliamentary majority. Given that we are still over 14 months away from the elections, and Morawiecki has not even yet officially split from PiS, it is still far too early to make confident predictions. However, while Morawiecki’s likely departure is clearly a personal blow to Kaczyński – and a sign of the 77-year-old’s waning influence over not only the Polish right but even his own party – it may conversely provide a boost to the opposition as a whole. Poland has banned children from using smartphones and other electronic devices in primary schools and kindergartens in a bid to improve their wellbeing and safety. The new legislation, signed into law by opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki on Thursday, will take effect at the start of the school year on 1 September, but schools will have until the end of 2026 to adjust. Prezydent podpisał nowelizację, która zakazuje korzystania z telefonów komórkowych w przedszkolach i szkołach. (PAP)#PAPInformacje pic.twitter.com/CK7YFU7sru — Polska Agencja Prasowa/Polish Press Agency (PAP) (@PAPinformacje) July 30, 2026 Under the new rules, pupils in primary schools and kindergartens will be prohibited from using smartphones and other electronic devices allowing communication or audio and video recording for the entire school day, including breaks and lessons held outside of school grounds. Schools will be allowed, but not required, to create designated places where pupils’ devices can be stored in a safe way and with respect for their privacy. The law, however, allows for some exceptions. When pupils need a device because of illness, disability or other special needs, school headteachers can permit their use. Phones could also be used in emergencies where there is a direct threat to life, health or property. Furthermore, pupils will be permitted to use mobile phones if a teacher deems them necessary for educational purposes and gives approval. The law also allows secondary schools to introduce bans on smartphone use if they choose, but does not make this compulsory, with such schools retaining autonomy to set their own rules through their statutes. The draft law banning phones from primary schools was first approved by the government in June. It then went to the Sejm, the lower and more powerful chamber of Poland’s parliament, which introduced amendments, including extending the measures to kindergartens. The Sejm then approved the bill in a rare near-unanimous vote, with only some MPs from the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja) voting against it. Subsequently, the Senate passed the bill without amendments, sending it to Nawrocki, who could have signed it, vetoed it, or sent it to Poland’s constitutional court for review. Poland’s government has approved a ban on mobile phones in primary schools as well as tougher age-verification requirements for online pornography. Both measures still require parliamentary and presidential approval before becoming law https://t.co/y4Ycf46FQD — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 2, 2026 The president ultimately decided to sign the law, with his office noting that the measures aim to “create safer learning conditions” and support the “healthy and responsible” use of digital technologies by pupils. Poland’s education minister Barbara Nowacka said last month that the law would “improve teachers’ power, autonomy and agency, as well as order and digital wellbeing in schools”. She added that, although many schools already have such bans in place, teachers had asked for legal backing to help enforce them. For more on the measures, see our earlier report from when the bill was approved almost unanimously by parliament, with only the far right voting against it https://t.co/9Mx0SfkE5V — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 17, 2026 According to a survey conducted in April by the Polish state research institute CBOS for the Polish Press Agency (PAP), 85% of Poles support a ban on the use of smartphones in primary schools. Poland has been recently stepping up efforts to protect young people from various digital threats. The topic has been a rare area of consensus between the government and Nawrocki, who has vetoed a record number of bills. Earlier this month, Nawrocki signed a law banning online content depicting illegal acts or other forms of abusive and degrading behaviour – known in Polish as “patostreaming”. Another measure approved by the government that is now being considered by parliament is the introduction of stricter age-verification requirements for accessing online pornography. In January, the digital affairs ministry also announced that it hoped to introduce measures blocking children from access to social media. Poland hopes this year to introduce measures preventing children from accessing social media, says the country's digital affairs ministry. Tomczyk said Poland was working closely with Ukraine, adding that 20 of the roughly 70 missiles fired by Russia overnight from Wednesday to Thursday were at one point heading towards Poland. “It is also worth noting that the vast majority of these missiles were shot down by Ukraine over Ukrainian territory, which clearly bore the full brunt of the attack,” he said. He added that a Ukrainian pilot had tracked the missile that later fell on Polish territory but was unable to intercept it. “He turned back 20 seconds before reaching the border,” Tomczyk said, adding that the pilot “could not have flown into” Polish airspace. He is banned from re-entering Poland and the Schengen area for five years. The 34-year-old was charged with promoting Nazism, an offence carrying a maximum sentence of three years in prison, and desecration of a memorial site. “A place that symbolises one of the greatest tragedies in human history requires special respect, and insulting it does not go without consequences,” said the border guard. @PolskaPolicja zatrzymała ob. A police probe found that the man, who had been living and working in the Wielkopolska province, had “posed for a photo making the Nazi salute” at the museum while visiting it. Prosecutors were informed of the case, police said, adding that the man was subsequently charged with two crimes: public promotion of Nazism and the desecration of a memorial site. He admitted to the offences and voluntarily submitted to his punishment, which consisted of a 2,000 zloty (€464) fine along with a decision for his verdict to be made public, they added. He was then handed over to Poland’s border guard, which decided to deport him and ban him from entering Poland and other Schengen countries for five years. The border guard said that the decision was “immediately enforceable”, and was based on “considerations of security and public order as well as the interests of the Republic of Poland.” It also noted that a court decided to place the man in a facility for foreigners in the city of Przemyśl, where he will await deportation. Poland’s government has appointed a marketing and branding expert to develop a unified strategy for promoting the country abroad, saying the move will help boost tourism, support Polish products and attract foreign investment. Barbara Mróz-Gorgoń, a professor at Wrocław University of Economics, noted that her appointment signals “a shift” from simple promotional activities to “managing the reputation of our great country”. The move comes as Poland seeks to capitalise on its economic success, including growth in tourism and continued investments. But the government says that current promotion efforts lack a single strategy and are fragmented. Czas na markę Polska! Witamy na pokładzie prof. Barbarę Mróz – Gorgoń 🇵🇱 pic.twitter.com/PPX2eWTRSm — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) July 29, 2026 Last year, Poland’s sport and tourism ministry appointed Mróz-Gorgoń, who also advises companies and institutions on branding strategy and founded a think tank dedicated to promoting Poland, to an interministerial team tasked with developing a comprehensive new branding strategy for Poland. The government said, however, that efforts to promote Poland were so far fragmented and lacked a single strategy, which is why it created the post of commissioner for promotion of the Poland brand. As the first specialist to take the position, Mróz-Gorgoń will be tasked with preparing a strategy to build a national brand and help implement it, coordinate activities to help grow tourism, support investments, and improve Poland’s position on the world stage. “We will create one programme resulting in the joint promotion of our country’s brand,” said Tusk. According to the government, this will come at no further cost, but ensure that existing funds will be spent in a more “coherent and effective way”. Mróz-Gorgoń, meanwhile, noted that “the Poland brand is not the property of the government. It is created by entrepreneurs, artists, athletes, local governments and millions of Poles at home and abroad”. Developing this brand “means more investment, recognition of our brands and products abroad, and it also provides greater strength in international relations,” she continued. Prime Minister Donald Tusk said on Thursday that Polish airspace had been violated during a massive missile attack by Russia on western Ukraine overnight, adding that there were no casualties or immediate threat to civilians. A suspected Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crashed in eastern Poland, around 100 km from the Ukrainian border, prompting the deployment of police counter-terrorism officers and other security services to the site. The fall of the object, which is reported to have caused a powerful explosion, left a crater about 10 metres wide and scattered fragments in a field between Tarnawa-Kolonia and Tokary in Lublin province, about 2 km from the nearest buildings, according to local police. World.title: World-Famous DJ Tiësto Returns to Prague on August 23
World.content:
Dutch DJ and producer Tiësto is returning to Prague on August 23, with a performance scheduled at DupleX Prague.

One of the most recognizable names in electronic music, Tiësto has been a major figure in the international dance scene for more than two decades. His Prague appearance will bring him back to the city for another night at the popular rooftop club in the centre of Prague.

The event is expected to feature a mix of Tiësto’s well-known tracks and newer material, alongside the production and atmosphere that have become a regular part of his live shows.

Tiësto, whose real name is Tijs Verwest, began his career in the Dutch club scene before becoming internationally known through his work in trance music.



Over the years, his sound has developed considerably, moving towards house, EDM and more mainstream dance music.

He has since performed at some of the world’s largest festivals and venues and worked with a wide range of artists. His music has also reached audiences well beyond the traditional electronic music scene, helping establish him as one of the genre’s most commercially successful artists.

Tickets are on sale through the official DupleX website.

New album

Tiësto is working on a new album that will see him return to his trance roots.

The Dutch DJ said he had recently “got re-inspired by trance music” and was gradually bringing the genre back into his sound. He said he hopes to finish the album soon.

The project follows “Bring Me To Life,” released last November as the first taste of what Tiësto said his 2026 album could sound like.

World.title: Spaniard Santi Denia Named Coach of the Czech Republic National Team
World.content:
Spanish coach Santi Denia took over the Czech Republic national team on Friday to become the first foreigner in the post.

The Czech soccer association said the 52-year-old signed a two-year contract with an option to be extended by another two years.

Czech football association head David Trunda introduced Denia at a news conference in Prague.

“We greatly appreciate that an expert with such a credit and immense experience at the international level is joining the Czech national team,” Trunda said.



“I’m happy to be here and I’m extremely motivated, because I consider it a great opportunity to lead the Czech national team,” Denia said. “Czech football has a magnificent history and I honestly regard it as a great honor to be here.”

Denia replaced Miroslav Koubek who resigned after the team’s early exit from the World Cup.

Denia was a center-back in Atletico Madrid (1994-2005) and has two games on the national team to his credit.

As coach, he led Spain to gold at the 2024 Paris Olympics. He also claimed the European titles with Spain´s under-17 (2017) and under-19 teams (2019).

He was most recently in charge of Al-Shahania, a club in Qatar.

His first major task in the post will be to face tough opponents in League A of the Nations League. The Czechs open the competition by hosting Croatia on Sept. 26 in a group which also includes England and World Cup champions Spain.

World.title: Czech PM Calls for Closing Schengen to Spain due to Migration Crisis in Ceuta
World.content:
Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš called for temporarily excluding Spain from Schengen due to the migration crisis in Ceuta, where about 49,000 migrants entered uncontrollably from Morocco.

Italy has already suspended Schengen rules in connection with Spain.

Czech Prime Minister Andrej Babiš called for closing the Schengen zone to Spain after a sharp escalation of the migration crisis in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta.

According to Babiš, the situation in Ceuta is “absolutely scandalous,” and the cause of the crisis was the overly lenient migration policy of the Spanish authorities.



According to the publication, since Thursday, about 49,000 migrants have entered Ceuta uncontrollably from the territory of Morocco. At least 19 people have died trying to cross the maritime border.

Foreign Minister Petr Macinka (Motorists) described the situation as a serious challenge for the entire Schengen Area but stopped short of calling for Spain’s exclusion, saying he wanted to hear Madrid’s position before drawing conclusions.

What is the Schengen Agreement?

The Schengen Area allows people to travel between 29 European countries without routine passport checks at internal borders.

While border controls are normally abolished, member states can temporarily reinstate them if they believe there is a serious threat to public order or internal security.

Italy does not share a land border with Spain, so the decision to reintroduce border controls for a month will impact people travelling by plane or boat between the two countries.

Where is Ceuta?

Ceuta is an autonomous Spanish city on the northern coast of Africa that borders Morocco.

Spain also controls the nearby city of Melilla. Together, the two enclaves form the European Union’s only land borders with Africa.

Roughly the size of inner Sydney, Ceuta has a population of just over 83,000, according to Spain’s Instituto Nacional de Estadistica. It is home to Christian and Muslim communities, including Spanish and Moroccan residents and cross-border workers.

World.title: Prague’s Online Heat Map Shows Where to Find Water and Shade
World.content:
As another spell of extreme summer heat approaches the Czech Republic, Prague has published an online map showing where residents can cool down, find drinking water or spend time near water.

Temperatures in the capital could reach 38°C, with the hottest conditions expected toward the end of the week.

This map is designed to help people find relief across the city and includes public drinking fountains, misting systems, fountains, wells and locations suitable for swimming or relaxing beside the water.

The project was prepared by the City of Prague in cooperation with the Prague Institute of Planning and Development (IPR Prague) and the municipal technology company Operátor ICT.



The initiative is part of the city’s broader efforts to prepare for more frequent periods of extreme heat. Prague says it is increasingly focusing on measures that can reduce the effects of rising temperatures over the longer term, rather than relying only on temporary interventions.

More trees, water and shade planned

Prague is also looking to incorporate more greenery and water into public spaces as part of new development projects.

The city is supporting measures including new fountains and other water features, green roofs, rainwater collection tanks, climbing plants, permeable surfaces and additional tree planting. The expansion of parks is also among the measures being considered.

Temperatures could approach 40°C

The current heatwave is expected to reach its peak on Friday, when temperatures could climb as high as 39°C in parts of the Czech Republic.

Friday night could also remain exceptionally warm, with overnight temperatures staying above 20°C in some areas.

A temporary change is expected on Saturday, particularly in parts of the country where showers and thunderstorms could bring some relief. The cooler conditions, however, are not expected to last.

At the beginning of next week, temperatures are forecast to rise again, with daytime highs between 32°C and 37°C.

World.title: Canadian International High School in Prague: Your Pathway to Top Universities Worldwide
World.content:
Earning an internationally recognized high school diploma and preparing for admission to top universities no longer requires moving abroad.

Canadian International High School in Prague (CIHS) offers students in Grades 10-12 a fully English-language education based on the Canadian curriculum.

Located in the heart of Prague, CIHS combines the strengths of Canada’s education system with the quality of life and accessibility of the Czech Republic. Students receive a globally recognized diploma while studying in a familiar European environment, avoiding the higher costs and challenges of relocating overseas.

An International Diploma Recognized Worldwide

Graduates earn the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD), Canada’s official high school credential, recognized in more than 20 countries. The diploma provides access to over 30,000 universities and colleges worldwide, including leading institutions across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Europe.

Unlike the Czech education system, which typically spans 13 years, the Canadian program is completed in 12. As a result, students graduate a year earlier, begin university sooner, and gain an additional advantage as they build their academic and professional future.

Learning the Canadian Way

CIHS delivers its academic program in partnership with Toronto Imperial School, ensuring that students follow authentic Canadian educational standards. Courses are taught using modern curricula, teaching methods, and learning resources aligned with those used in Ontario schools.

English is the language of instruction across all subjects. An international faculty, including teachers from Canada, creates an immersive English-speaking environment that helps students strengthen their academic language skills and confidently transition into universities abroad.

To maintain high academic standards, all teachers undergo a rigorous selection process followed by professional training led by Canadian educators and the school’s academic partners.

Outstanding Value

Tuition is, on average, two to three times lower than at many international schools in Prague while offering an extensive range of included benefits.

Tuition covers:

the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD)

an iPad for both academic and personal use

for both academic and personal use a complete school uniform

an annual gym membership

continuous academic guidance and support

and support educational trips to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and Germany

to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and Germany participation in the Exchange program in the United States.

International Experience Beyond the Classroom

Education at CIHS extends well beyond the classroom. Each semester, students have the opportunity to join educational trips to Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Switzerland, and other destinations. These experiences include university campus visits, meetings with admissions representatives, and valuable insight into international higher education systems.

Students may also participate in the Exchange USA program, spending one or two semesters at one of 40 partner high schools across the United States. The program offers full immersion in American school life while strengthening English proficiency and developing valuable intercultural experience.

For students planning to continue their education in the U.S., CIHS also offers the opportunity to transfer to an American high school during Grade 12 on an F-1 student visa, complete their final year there, and graduate with a U.S. high school diploma.

A Modern Campus in Central Prague

The school is located in Holešovice, one of Prague’s fastest-growing and most vibrant districts. Its central location makes the campus easily accessible from virtually any part of the city by public transportation, while convenient parking is available for families.

The campus occupies a modern business complex close to parks and the Vltava riverfront, providing an ideal balance between study and recreation. Students also benefit from an on-site cafeteria and access to medical professionals, including general practitioners, dermatologists, immunologists, and allergists. Sports facilities, swimming pools, cafés, and shops are all within walking distance.

Personalized University Preparation

Beginning after Grade 10, students choose one of two academic pathways: Business & Social Science or Engineering, allowing them to focus on subjects aligned with their future university studies.

Throughout the program, experienced teachers and academic advisors provide personalized guidance, helping students develop essential academic skills, explore career options, and build competitive university applications.

Graduate Outcomes

By the time they graduate, CIHS students have gained far more than a high school diploma. They leave with:

the internationally recognized Ontario Secondary School Diploma

strong academic English proficiency

experience studying in an international environment

university admissions guidance

a global network of peers

participation in international educational programs

access to leading universities across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and beyond.

Canadian International High School in Prague welcomes prospective students and their families to visit the campus, meet the faculty, and learn more about its Canadian curriculum.

It’s an opportunity to experience a truly international education and earn a globally recognized diploma – while staying in the heart of Europe.

World.title: Prague Pride Strengthens Security Measures Following Berlin Attack
World.content:
Security will be tightened at this year’s Prague Pride festival following a deadly attack at a similar event in Berlin.

Czech police are preparing additional measures to protect participants in the week-long festival, which begins Monday.

The measures will also reflect changes to this year’s festival route and venue.

Prague Pride is moving its main festival area from Letná Plain to Štvanice Island. The traditional Saturday parade will also follow a new route, starting in the lower section of Wenceslas Square, continuing through the historic center and ending at Štvanice.



Organizers will begin the parade with a minute of silence on Wenceslas Square to remember the person killed in the Berlin attack.

“Thousands of people standing in silence will be a reminder that we will definitely not remain silent about violence motivated by prejudice,” Prague Pride director Kamila Fröhlichová said.

This year’s Prague Pride will feature more than 100 cultural, educational and social events. Dozens of associations, institutions, companies and individuals will organize programs at venues across the capital.

While many events will focus on the lives and experiences of LGBTQ+ people, the festival will also address wider questions surrounding human rights and civil society. A full program is available on the Prague Pride website.

Prague Pride was first held in August 2011. Its inaugural edition was met with strong opposition from conservative groups and politicians, who described the parade as obscene and accused its organizers of promoting what they called an “ideology of homosexuality.”

Then-President Václav Klaus was among the most prominent critics, arguing that society needed to oppose what he described as the spread of homosexuality.

Protests continued in subsequent years but gradually declined in size and intensity.

World.title: Prague Opens Air-Conditioned Space in City Centre to Help Beat Heat Wave
World.content:
People looking for relief from the heat in central Prague can use the air-conditioned ground floor of the Škoda Palace in Jungmannova Street on Thursday and Friday.

The city has opened the space to the public as temperatures across the Czech Republic are expected to rise well above 30°C. The building will be accessible from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. on both days.

Visitors can sit on benches and chairs, refill their water bottles at drinking fountains and use the toilets. Drinks and snacks are also available for purchase.



The measure comes as the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute has warned of very high temperatures in parts of the country. Forecasters are advising people to drink regularly, stay out of direct sunlight where possible and avoid strenuous physical activity, particularly during the afternoon.

The Czech Republic is facing several days of intense heat, with Friday expected to be among the hottest day of the current spell. Temperatures above 35°C are possible in some areas.

Individual Prague districts are taking similar steps. Prague 3, for example, plans to make air-conditioned areas in its town hall, information centre and Žižkostel available to the public when temperatures are forecast to exceed 35°C. Visitors will be able to sit down, drink water and take a break from the heat.

The city says the cooling spaces are intended to provide temporary relief during the hottest periods, particularly for people who may struggle to cope with high temperatures.

World.title: Revolut Opens Private Market Funds to Czech Investors
World.content:
Revolut is expanding its investment services in the Czech Republic, giving retail customers access to funds focused on private equity, private credit and infrastructure.

The new products will become available in the Revolut app from July 31. The fintech has signed distribution agreements with four major asset managers — Apollo, Ares, Hamilton Lane and Partners Group — which collectively manage more than $2.8 trillion in assets.

The move gives Czech retail investors access to parts of the private markets that have traditionally been aimed largely at institutional investors.



Private market investments have often required substantial minimum commitments, frequently above €100,000, or around CZK 2.5 million. Revolut’s new offering is designed to lower that barrier and allow customers to add private assets to portfolios that may already include stocks, bonds and exchange-traded funds.

Investments will be available directly through the Revolut app.

The funds will be offered through the European Long-Term Investment Fund framework, known as ELTIF 2.0.

How ELTIF 2.0 works

The structure is intended to provide investors with greater flexibility than traditional private equity funds, where capital can remain committed for several years and withdrawals may not be possible during that period.

The products offered through Revolut use an “evergreen” structure. This allows investors to put money into funds with existing portfolios rather than waiting for a traditional investment cycle to begin.

ELTIF 2.0 also provides scheduled liquidity windows during which investors can request the redemption of their holdings, subject to the conditions of the individual fund.

That does not mean the investments are as liquid as publicly traded shares. Private market assets remain difficult to sell quickly, and investors should expect to hold their money for the long term.

Revolut already offers Czech customers access to a range of traditional investments, including US and European stocks, ETFs, bonds and commodities. The addition of private market funds expands the investment options available through the same app.

World.title: These were the most-watched FIFA World Cup matches in Hungary
World.content:
Never before in the history of the FIFA World Cup have there been as many matches as there were in 2026. A total of 104 matches were played, most of which Hungarian viewers could watch on M4 Sport, while a few matches were broadcast on the Duna World channel due to overlapping events at the end of the group stage. Two weeks after the World Cup, it’s worth looking back at which matches drew the largest audiences, based on viewership data.

The World Cup final was the most-watched program of the year so far

According to data from Nielsen Közönségmérés Kft., the final—in which Spain defeated Argentina 1–0 after extra time—drew an average of 1,502,352 viewers across the entire population via television. This made the broadcast on M4 Sport the most-watched TV program of 2026 so far, at least when considering only linear broadcasts; after all, the event could also be followed online on the M4 Sport website and on Médiaklik. In the case of the online platforms, the public broadcaster reported an audience of 227,000 on the day following the World Cup final.

Interestingly, only two other television programs in Hungary have come close to this figure so far this year. On January 1, TV2 reached 1,468,431 viewers with the film *How Could I Live Without You?*. Many believed even then that no channel would achieve higher viewership than this throughout the year, but ultimately, RTL also came close with its broadcast of the UEFA Champions League final in Budapest. An average of 1,430,219 viewers tuned in to watch the match on television, which is a truly outstanding figure, but it wasn’t quite enough to break the record set up to that point. However, the picture is somewhat nuanced by the fact that many people watched the Champions League final via the RTL+ streaming service; based on linear TV viewership figures, though, we had to wait until the World Cup to reach 1.5 million viewers.

What about the other matches?

As the World Cup heated up, the matches attracted increasing attention. An average of 1,027,898 people across the entire population tuned in to the England-Argentina semifinal, placing the match—broadcast by M4 Sport—in second place on the Week 29 viewership chart, though it also took the bottom spot on the podium that week. The excitement of the bronze medal match between France and England drew 636,658 viewers despite the late start time, so it wasn’t just the fact that the English won 6–4 and a total of 10 goals were scored that piqued so many people’s interest afterward.

However, the bronze medal match still didn’t make the top three when compared to the viewership numbers of other World Cup matches. The round of 16 match between Portugal and Spain was the week’s top-rated game with 937,407 viewers. Behind that, the Spain-Belgium quarterfinal took fourth place on the overall World Cup viewership list (731,277 viewers), while the fifth-most-watched match was the Brazil-Norway clash (647,949 viewers). This round of 16 match proved sufficient for M4 Sport to win the ratings race for the entire 27th week.

In the six weeks since the World Cup began, there was only one instance during the group stage when a non-World Cup match topped the relevant lists. In Week 25, for example, RTL’s and TV2’s news programs both outperformed the live broadcast of the group stage match between Portugal and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The latter was watched by an average of 570,163 viewers across the entire population, but there were matches during the group stage that generated even higher viewership figures.

World.title: Car crashes into Budapest tram stop, smashing glass shelter
World.content:
A car crashed into a tram stop at Blaha Lujza Square in central Budapest on Sunday evening, shattering one of the shelter’s large glass panels and triggering an emergency response.

According to Hungary’s National Directorate General for Disaster Management, the incident occurred in Budapest’s 8th district, where a passenger vehicle ploughed into the tram stop.

Glass shelter destroyed in the collision

The impact completely shattered a large glass panel at the busy public transport stop. Emergency medical services were called to assist a passenger who had been waiting at the tram stop when the crash occurred. Authorities have not yet released information about the person’s condition or whether anyone else was injured.

Firefighters secured the scene

Professional firefighters from Budapest were dispatched to the location and disconnected the vehicle’s battery to eliminate any electrical hazards. The circumstances leading to the crash have not yet been disclosed, and authorities have not provided further details about what caused the driver to lose control.

The incident occurred at one of Budapest’s busiest transport hubs, where several tram and bus lines intersect.

World.title: Will Hungary’s energy crisis derail Sziget Festival? Organisers reveal emergency power plan
World.content:
As Hungary prepares for a critical week amid an unprecedented energy crisis, many festivalgoers have been wondering whether the country’s biggest music event could be affected. Sziget Festival organisers have now addressed those concerns, insisting that the event will go ahead even if the national electricity grid experiences disruptions.

According to a statement published by the festival, Sziget operates its own generator-based power supply system, allowing it to function independently of Hungary’s electricity network if necessary.

“If required, we can completely disconnect from the national power grid and generate all the electricity needed for the festival ourselves,” the organisers said.

They added that this means the festival places no additional burden on Hungary’s electricity system while ensuring both visitor safety and uninterrupted operations.

Energy-efficient upgrades have reduced consumption

Organisers also highlighted that the festival’s energy demand has been steadily declining thanks to years of technological improvements.

Modern LED lighting, energy-efficient sound systems and other infrastructure upgrades have significantly reduced electricity consumption. They added that they continue to explore further ways to lower energy use without compromising visitor experience or safety.

The announcement comes as the Hungarian government has called on businesses and institutions across the country to minimise electricity consumption following the partial shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant caused by exceptionally low Danube water levels.

Sustainability measures extend beyond electricity

Sziget also stressed its environmental efforts in other areas. Free drinking water refill stations will once again be available throughout the festival site, encouraging visitors to use reusable bottles instead of single-use plastics.

To reduce dust, water sprayed across the grounds naturally filters back into the Danube through the gravel beneath Óbuda Island, allowing it to re-enter the natural water cycle. Organisers said they continue to seek new ways to reduce the festival’s overall environmental footprint.

Festival to go ahead as planned

The organisers concluded by reaffirming that safety, responsible operation and sustainability remain among Sziget’s core priorities.

The festival is scheduled to take place on Budapest’s Óbuda Island from 11 to 15 August, with organisers stating that visitors can expect the event to proceed as planned despite the ongoing national energy challenges.

World.title: Hungary calls cross-party crisis talks over heatwave and energy situation
World.content:
Ágnes Forsthoffer, who is temporarily exercising the powers of Hungary’s President, has called an urgent meeting with Prime Minister Péter Magyar and the leaders of all parliamentary party groups to discuss the country’s worsening heatwave, water shortages and the impact of the shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant.

According to a statement issued by Sándor Palace on Sunday, the meeting will take place on Monday morning.

Hungary’s government asked to explain crisis response

The statement said Forsthoffer had requested an urgent and extraordinary briefing from the Prime Minister on the current situation caused by the extreme heat and on the measures the government has already taken, as well as those planned for the coming days.

Sándor Palace described the combination of the prolonged heatwave, the critically low water level of the River Danube, the shutdown of the Paks Nuclear Power Plant and third-degree water restrictions affecting several municipalities as an exceptional situation requiring immediate and coordinated action.

Parliamentary party leaders invited

As the National Assembly is not scheduled to hold an extraordinary plenary session next week, Forsthoffer said it was important that the leaders of the parliamentary groups receive information directly from the Prime Minister and have an opportunity to ask questions.

The acting head of state also announced the initiative on her official Facebook page, expressing hope for the cooperation of all political parties. Prime Minister Péter Magyar responded publicly, thanking Forsthoffer for the invitation.

Prime Minister stresses importance of national unity

In a video message published on Sunday, Magyar confirmed that he would first brief Forsthoffer before meeting parliamentary group leaders at Sándor Palace. He said he would provide detailed information on both the challenges inherited by his government and the decisions and measures taken in response to the current situation.

The Prime Minister of Hungary argued that, in a crisis of this scale, national unity and open dialogue between the government, political parties and society are essential for an effective response.

Stay up-to-date: Hungary braces for 40°C heatwave after record-warm night

Opposition parties confirm attendance

Opposition party Fidesz confirmed that it would attend Monday’s briefing. János Bóka, the party’s parliamentary group leader, said Fidesz was expecting detailed information about the government’s planned measures to address the energy crisis.

The KDNP also announced that it would participate in the meeting, saying every necessary measure should be taken in the interests of the Hungarian people. The party also thanked emergency workers and the public for their efforts and perseverance during the ongoing crisis.

Monday’s meeting comes as Hungary continues to grapple with one of its most severe heatwaves in recent years, with extreme temperatures, water shortages and energy supply challenges placing increasing pressure on the country’s infrastructure and public services.

Read also: Péter Magyar says Paks Nuclear Power Plant will shut down completely very soon

World.title: Hungary braces for 40°C heatwave after record-warm night
World.content:
Hungary is set to endure another day of the extreme summer heatwave, with temperatures expected to climb as high as 40°C on Sunday after the country experienced a record-warm night.

According to the latest forecast from HungaroMet, most of the country will enjoy sunny or only slightly cloudy skies, although isolated showers and thunderstorms may develop later in the day in parts of the North Hungarian Mountains and the Transdanubian Mountains.

Heatwave soaring to 40°C

Afternoon highs are forecast to range between 34°C and 40°C, while even after sunset temperatures are expected to remain exceptionally high, falling to only 25–32°C by late evening.

Winds will generally be light to moderate, although stronger north-easterly breezes are possible in some areas. Any thunderstorms that develop could be accompanied by temporary gale-force wind gusts of 60–70 km/h, small hail and intense downpours.

Record-breaking tropical night

The intense heatwave follows an exceptionally warm night from Saturday into Sunday. HungaroMet reported that its weather station on János Hill in Budapest recorded a minimum temperature of 26°C, making it the warmest dawn on record for this date. For comparison, the previous record was a “mere” 24.9°C.

Across much of the country, average daily temperatures on Saturday reached or exceeded 29°C. Saturday’s daytime maximum also came close to breaking the national record, highlighting the severity of the ongoing heatwave.

Heat warning remains in force

HungaroMet has maintained its warning for persistently high average daily temperatures. On both Sunday and Monday, average temperatures are expected to remain above 29°C across most of Hungary, while areas near the north-eastern and south-western borders are forecast to see daily averages of 27–29°C.

Meteorologists also warn that isolated thunderstorms may develop again on Monday, particularly in the North Hungarian Mountains and possibly central parts of the country. These storms could bring strong wind gusts, small hail and locally heavy rainfall.

Authorities urge caution

With temperatures remaining dangerously high both during the day and overnight, authorities continue to advise residents and visitors to stay hydrated, avoid prolonged exposure to direct sunlight during the hottest hours, and take extra care of children, elderly people and those with chronic health conditions.

The prolonged tropical nights, during which temperatures remain unusually high after dark, also increase the health risks associated with the ongoing heatwave.

Péter Magyar: The next five days are going to be the most critical

Following the shutdown of the Paks nuclear power plant and amid the extreme heatwave, Hungary will be entering its “most critical five-day period”, Prime Minister Peter Magyar said on Sunday.

In a video message posted on Facebook, the prime minister said that starting Monday, the Paks plant will produce no electricity at all, while the country was facing the hottest days, with temperatures reaching 40°C.

People need to use the least possible amount of electricity

As a result, the electricity system, public services and the population will face enormous strain, he warned. Magyar urged everyone to pay even closer attention to vulnerable groups, such as children, the elderly, the sick, and those living alone, from Monday.

He also called for even more conscious electricity conservation between 5 PM and 10 PM, particularly between 6 PM and 9 PM, asking businesses, institutions, local councils and individuals to significantly reduce or postpone their power consumption during this window.

Read also: Budapest smashes 105-year heat record as brutal heatwave tightens grip on Hungary

World.title: Hungarian man arrested after single-handedly shutting down Croatian airport
World.content:
Croatian police have arrested a 36-year-old Hungarian man on suspicion of causing major disruption at Split Airport by allegedly flying a drone without authorisation near the runway.

Air traffic suspended over safety concerns

The incident, which took place on Friday evening, temporarily brought air traffic at Split’s Saint Jerome Airport to a standstill, resulting in cancelled flights and significant delays for several others.

According to Croatian media reports, the suspected unauthorised drone flight near the airport’s runway forced airport authorities to suspend all flight operations while the potential threat to air safety was assessed.

Police launch criminal proceedings against Hungarian man

The temporary closure led to the cancellation of two flights, while several others experienced lengthy delays before services could resume.

Officers from the Split-Dalmatia Police Administration quickly launched an investigation against the Hungarian man after receiving reports on Friday, 31 July, that the safety of the airspace had been compromised.

Budapest Airport unveils huge expansion plans

Budapest Airport has launched one of the largest planning tenders in its history, laying the groundwork for a comprehensive, long-term redevelopment of Budapest Liszt Ferenc International Airport.

The ambitious programme includes a brand-new terminal, additional passenger piers, a railway station, new roads, parking facilities and extensive upgrades across the airport’s infrastructure.

According to procurement documents published in the European Union’s TED public procurement database and shared by Magyar Építők, the airport operator is seeking to conclude framework agreements with several design firms for a period of 96 months.

The tender is intended to prepare a comprehensive development programme rather than a single construction project.

Read also: Budapest taxi fares rise from today – airport pickups also become more expensive

World.title: Tragedy: Two festivalgoers die at Ozora Festival in Hungary
World.content:
Two people have died during this year’s Ozora Festival in central Hungary, including a 45-year-old American man whose death is being investigated by police and a 39-year-old woman who suffered sudden cardiac arrest.

According to the Fejér County Police Headquarters, the fatal incident involving the American national occurred at around 4 PM on Saturday, 1 August.

Festival organisers alerted the authorities after the man climbed onto decorative structures surrounding the main stage before falling to his death, reports Telex.

Police rule out foul play

The Sárbogárd Police Department has launched an administrative investigation to establish the exact circumstances of the incident.

Police said they have ruled out the involvement of a third party. Based on the evidence gathered so far, investigators believe the death was likely the result of suicide.

Further details are expected following a press conference scheduled for Sunday afternoon, where Ozora Festival’s chief organiser and owner, Árpád Zimányi, is due to address the incident.

Second fatality at the festival

In a statement published on its official Facebook page, the festival also confirmed a second death.

A 39-year-old woman suffered sudden cardiac arrest during the event. Emergency medical teams arrived at the scene within minutes and attempted resuscitation but were unable to save her life.

Music programme shortened

Following the two tragic incidents, festival organisers announced that all musical performances on Sunday would end at midnight.

They also reminded attendees that a heat alert remains in force and urged visitors to take appropriate precautions in the extreme temperatures.

The Ozora Festival, one of Europe’s best-known psychedelic music and arts events, attracts thousands of visitors from around the world each year.

Read also: World’s third public statue of Freddie Mercury unveiled on Lake Balaton – but it bears a striking resemblance to a Hungarian poet

World.title: Péter Magyar: Paks Nuclear Power Plant to shut down completely
World.content:
The penultimate generating unit at the Paks Nuclear Power Plant was taken offline at 1.30 AM on Sunday due to the continued fall in the Danube’s water level, Prime Minister Péter Magyar announced on his Facebook page late on Saturday night.

The power plant is generating a fraction of its capacity

Prime Minister Péter Magyar highlighted that the plant is now generating only 240 megawatts and that “tomorrow, for the first time in 44 years, it will be shut down completely.” Under normal operating conditions, the Paks Nuclear Power Plant has a generating capacity of 2,000 megawatts.

Earlier on Saturday, Péter Magyar said that, due to the significant reduction in Hungary’s power generation capacity, the Hungarian Independent Transmission Operator (MAVIR) had activated its emergency protocol for major disruptions to the electricity system.

He stated that all available reserve power plants across Hungary were in operation or on standby, including facilities that had long been out of service and were in extremely poor condition. All power plants capable of being brought online have been supplied with the necessary fuel.

Péter Magyar: Large consumers that fail to meet their commitments may face sanctions

Under a government decree that entered into force on Saturday evening, major industrial electricity consumers may be disconnected from the power grid if they fail to implement the required reductions in electricity consumption. Prime Minister Péter Magyar said:

“Households are at the very end of the restriction chain. The burden will first be borne by the state, large corporations, industrial facilities and institutions with deferrable energy consumption. The system operator may only interfere with the electricity supply of Hungarian households once every other option has been exhausted. This is what systemic change looks like in practice.”

As part of the government’s energy-saving measures, rail freight services will be suspended during the most critical period between 5 PM and 10 PM from Monday onwards. In addition, remote working will be introduced for the first three days of next week across all public administration roles where the continuous delivery of services allows.

Those able to work remotely are asked to do so

The government has also called on private-sector companies and employers to allow employees whose work can be carried out remotely to work from home over the coming days, while reducing energy consumption in office buildings to the lowest practicable level.

Péter Magyar also announced that decorative and non-essential lighting at all state institutions will be switched off, and that all local authorities across Hungary are expected to implement the highest possible level of energy-saving measures.

Stay up-to-date: Slovakian PM Fico offers to help Hungary with electricity as Paks shutdown threatens energy supply

Dunamenti Power Plant back in operation

Thanks to rapid repair work, the Dunamenti Power Plant in Százhalombatta resumed operations after three days, the Prime Minister announced on his Facebook page on Saturday afternoon. Péter Magyar noted that this adds a further 360 megawatts of generating capacity to the system and thanked everyone involved in the repair work.

In a statement posted on social media on Saturday, the Dunamenti Power Plant said that, following the successful completion of technical inspections and trial operation, the plant’s G3 generating unit resumed full-capacity operation at 4.45 PM on 1 August. As a result, nearly 400 megawatts of generating capacity has once again become available to Hungary’s electricity system.

The statement recalled that the planned restart of the G3 unit on 29 July had to be suspended after a technical fault was detected in a specialised seal on one of the steam turbine’s safety valves. The power plant emphasised that, thanks to the swift and well-coordinated efforts of its employees and technical partners, the unit was able to return to service safely in the shortest possible time.

Read also: Hungary to suspend freight trains during evening peak to save electricity amid energy crisis

World.title: Nscale to acquire Romanian co-founded AI startup Anyscale in reportedly USD 1.65 billion deal
World.content:
Cloud infrastructure provider Nscale will acquire AI software startup Anyscale, which has Romanian-born university professor Ion Stoica among its co-founders, in a transaction worth roughly USD 1.65 billion, according to a Bloomberg News source.

Ion Stoica is a co-founder of Anyscale, together with Robert Nishihara (chief executive officer) and Philipp Moritz (chief technology officer), who were his PhD students at RISELab within the University of California, Berkeley.

San Francisco-based Anyscale provides software for organizing and managing complex AI workloads so that they can run smoothly across multiple computers simultaneously. Nscale said it expects to attract more customers by offering Anyscale’s software.

Anyscale will continue to operate under its own brand and serve its existing customers, the companies said. Anyscale’s entire team of approximately 200 people across the United States, Europe and India will join Nscale as part of the acquisition.

The transaction is expected to be completed in the second half of this year, the companies said.

Anyscale recorded revenue growth of 70% compared with the previous quarter in the company’s most recent quarter, according to a blog post by its co-founders.

Originally from Romania, Stoica left for the United States in the late 1990s to pursue his PhD at Carnegie Mellon University. Since 2000, he has been teaching at UC Berkeley, where he leads a laboratory funded largely by technology companies such as Microsoft, Nvidia, Google, and IBM, with an annual budget of more than USD 6 million.

Stoica became a billionaire by launching four startups that originated from his research laboratory at the University of California, Berkeley. The most valuable of them, Databricks and Anyscale, started as open-source projects within the university. The first was valued at USD 134 billion earlier this year.

Before Databricks, Stoica also co-founded video streaming startup Conviva.

World.title: UNICEF, Romanian Labor Ministry launch e-Learning HUB for professionals in social assistance
World.content:
Romania’s Labor Ministry and UNICEF announced the launch of e-Learning HUB, a national platform dedicated to the continuous professional training of personnel in the field of social services and sectors that contribute to social inclusion.

The HUB provides coordinated access to training opportunities, educational resources and professional development programs. The platform brings together continuous professional training opportunities for specialists in the social field, covering essential topics such as the protection of vulnerable persons, human rights, digital skills and quality standards in social services.

The HUB is designed to become the digital foundation of the future National Center for Continuous Training in Social Assistance, which is scheduled to become operational in 2028. The platform will contribute to increasing the skills of professionals in social assistance and related fields, personnel of central and local public authorities with responsibilities in the social field, decision-makers, accredited professional training providers, professional organizations, and non-governmental organizations active in the field of social assistance and the protection of human rights.

“Through e-Learning HUB, specialists across the country will be able to identify relevant courses more easily, develop their skills and have access to modern resources adapted to the real needs of the system,” said Silvia Dinică, State Secretary within the Labor Ministry.

“Professionals in social services are facing increasingly complex challenges, from poverty and social exclusion to the effects of recent crises on children and families. The e-Learning HUB platform offers a single access point to quality learning opportunities and represents an important step toward strengthening the workforce in the social field,” said Anna Riatti, UNICEF Representative in Romania.

The e-Learning HUB will facilitate access to accredited training programs, promote collaboration between institutions and training providers, and support the development of the skills needed to provide integrated and quality services.

World.title: North Bucharest Investments ANALYSIS | ANCPI Disruptions Slow the Market, but Housing Demand Remains Strong
World.content:
News from Companies

Against the backdrop of the ongoing operational disruption affecting Romania's National Agency for Cadastre and Land Registration (ANCPI), which continues to slow the completion of real estate transactions, North Bucharest Investments' latest analysis shows that demand across the residential market remains strong. Approximately 40% of end-buyers are looking for houses, villas and large apartments, while studios and one-bedroom apartments account for 48% of all properties viewed and saved in the North Bucharest app.

Romania's residential market continues to be driven by genuine demand, while buyer profiles and purchasing preferences continue to evolve. Based on aggregated data from the North Bucharest app and the company's commercial activity over the past few months, North Bucharest Investments' latest analysis highlights two key trends shaping today's market: growing demand for spacious homes intended for owner-occupation and strengthening investment demand from Romanians living abroad.



According to the analysis, approximately 40% of active end-buyers are currently searching for houses, villas and large apartments, typically within a budget range of €600,000 to €800,000. This category of buyers primarily values space, comfort, construction quality and premium locations, making them less sensitive to short-term market fluctuations.



At the same time, North Bucharest Investments has observed steadily increasing interest from Romanians living abroad, who continue to return to Romania's residential market with investment objectives. Most are focusing on studios and one-bedroom apartments, recognising their strong rental potential and long-term capital appreciation.



This trend is also reflected in user behaviour within the North Bucharest app, where 48% of all properties viewed and saved over the recent period are studios and one-bedroom apartments, making them the platform's most popular property category.

World.title: Bucharest Community Foundation and City Hall begin transforming Herăstrău Park through public-private collaboration
World.content:
Bucharest City Hall and the Bucharest Community Foundation announced on Friday, July 31, that they have begun transforming the city’s major northern park, Herăstrău, according to the priorities expressed by nearly 10,000 participants in the public consultation.

The process benefits from private funding worth EUR 900,000 already mobilized by the Bucharest Community Foundation. The first EUR 90,000 will be invested in the studies and expertise required for the regeneration of the park’s green spaces, with the remainder to be directed as the stages are established together with the public administration.

The funds will cover the tree inventory through a TreePlotter-type digital application, the creation of a public inventory, specialized studies, technical and dendrological expertise, assessment of tree health and risk, preparation of the tree management plan, as well as the documentation needed to establish design requirements for future interventions.

The digital tree inventory will be public and accessible both to the administration and citizens and will form the basis of a Green Register dedicated to Old Herăstrău Park. For each tree, GIS location, dendrometric characteristics, health status, and management recommendations will be recorded. Data can be permanently updated by the public administration, and the tool can be gradually expanded to the entire Herăstrău Park, providing a permanent instrument for monitoring and adaptive and sustainable management of tree heritage.

The two partners began working together through a new collaboration model that brings together public administration, the community, specialists and private funders. The new working mechanism allows preparatory stages to begin quickly, independently of the public budget calendar, while maintaining decision-making, control and ownership of the documentation within the public administration.

The Bucharest Community Foundation will finance and contract specialists for the regeneration of green spaces based on specifications agreed with the authorities and experts involved, while the results will be handed over to the Bucharest City Hall and will serve as the basis for future design and construction works.

Meanwhile, the two partners will prepare the administrative framework for major interventions and mobilize the private sector and civil society to attract the financial resources necessary for the subsequent stages of the regeneration process. Private resources will accelerate project preparation without transferring decision-making rights over the park to funders. Control, validation and ownership of documentation will remain the responsibility of the public administration, while intervention solutions and priorities will be defined in collaboration with specialists, funders and community members, in accordance with the principles of the New European Bauhaus.

Going forward, the Bucharest Community Foundation aims to attract funds of up to EUR 10 million from the private sector and civil society for the subsequent intervention plan.

“If we waited for the completion of administrative procedures for landscape design, as well as for securing the lakeside area, we would not have enough speed. That is why I cannot sufficiently emphasize the role of the Bucharest Community Foundation. My role was to be open to collaboration and, together, to create this mechanism through which we can get on track, set things in motion, and accelerate interventions,” said Bucharest mayor Ciprian Ciucu.

Public consultation

The planned works follow a public consultation carried out between May and June 2026, in which nearly half of respondents said that they were dissatisfied with the current state of the park.

Participants’ expectations were very concrete. Modernization of general infrastructure was considered a priority by 83.2% of respondents, while 74.3% indicated the restoration of the natural environment as one of the main intervention directions. Permanent public toilets, more numerous and cleaner, represented the most requested specific measure resulting from the consultation, indicated by 85.5% of respondents. Better lighting at night was desired by 81.4% of respondents, followed by the rehabilitation of paths and paving (77.9%), ensuring functional drinking fountains (68.9%) and improving urban furniture (61.6%).

Restoring the natural environment was equally important. Among the respondents, 78.6% requested more trees and denser vegetation for shade, cooling and air filtration, while 71.2% wanted improved lake water quality, and 56.9% wanted better access to the waterfront. Nearly half of participants mentioned degraded paths and sidewalks among the main complaints, while responses indicate a clear preference for preserving the park’s natural character and avoiding excessive interventions.

World.title: Over 6 in 10 Romanians cannot afford a one-week annual vacation
World.content:
Romania ranks first in the European Union in terms of the share of people who cannot afford a one-week annual vacation away from home, according to data published by Eurostat on Thursday, July 30.

According to the European Statistical Office, 61.4% of Romanians aged 16 or older said they could not afford a one-week vacation away from home in 2025. Romania is followed by Greece, where 46.6% of residents were in the same situation, and by Bulgaria and Hungary, both with 39.1%.

The difference from the European Union average is significant. Across the 27 member states, 27.5% of people aged over 16 said they could not afford a one-week holiday away from home.

Compared with 2024, the share of people who cannot afford a vacation increased by 0.5% across the European Union. However, the long-term trend remains positive. Compared with 2015, the indicator has fallen by 7.7%, so over the last decade more and more Europeans have gained the financial ability to go on holiday for at least one week a year.

At the other end of the ranking are the states where an annual vacation is accessible to the vast majority of the population. The lowest share of people unable to afford a one-week holiday was recorded in Luxembourg, where only 10.6% of residents said they could not cover such an expense. It is followed by Sweden, with 12.4%, and the Netherlands, with 12.8%, values almost five times lower than those reported in Romania.

The ability to spend at least one week a year on vacation away from home is one of the indicators used by Eurostat to assess living conditions and the level of material deprivation in the member states. The data highlight the persistent differences between European economies in terms of purchasing power and households’ ability to cover expenses considered normal for a decent standard of living.

World.title: Romania launches national campaign to promote its 13 national parks
World.content:
The Ministry of Environment and the Conservation Carpathia Foundation have launched a nationwide campaign to promote Romania’s 13 national parks and raise public awareness about their environmental and economic value. The campaign, titled Parks for Generations (Parcurile Generațiilor), was launched during the Făgăraș Fest festival and will run on television, radio, and digital platforms.

The initiative seeks to explain the difference between national parks and other natural or urban parks, encouraging Romanians to visit the protected areas while highlighting their role in biodiversity conservation, climate resilience, and local development.

Romania's 13 national parks protect around 317,500 hectares of land, including forests, alpine meadows, gorges, and caves that provide habitats for numerous rare plant and animal species. According to Conservation Carpathia, the parks also help regulate water cycles, reduce the risks of droughts and floods, and support local economies through tourism-related activities.

The national parks are Buila-Vânturarița, Călimani, Ceahlău, Bicaz Gorges-Hășmaș, Nera Gorges-Beușnița, Cozia, Jiu Gorge, Domogled-Cerna Valley, Măcin Mountains, Rodna Mountains, Piatra Craiului, Retezat, and Semenic-Caraș Gorges.

The campaign follows research showing that public understanding of national parks remains limited. A 2024 study by Unlock Market Research found that while 67% of Romanians said they had visited a national park, many confused them with nature reserves, natural parks, or other protected areas. Another finding showed that 82% of respondents could not define what distinguishes a national park from other forms of nature protection.

“National parks are among the most remarkable places Romania has. They protect nature, but they also create opportunities for local communities and future generations," said Barbara and Christoph Promberger, executive directors of the Conservation Carpathia Foundation.

“We want more Romanians to discover them, understand their value and be proud that Romania has such a rich natural heritage. People protect what they know and appreciate, and that is the first step we want to take together," they added.

In her turn, interim environment minister Diana Buzoianu said the campaign aims to address the public's limited knowledge of Romania’s protected areas.

“Romania has national parks with almost a century of history. […] Yet recent data show that too few Romanians know what a national park really is and the role it plays for nature, climate, water, local communities, and the economy," the minister said.

“The Parks for Generations campaign does exactly this: it brings national parks closer to the public and explains, in accessible language, why these places are so important for Romania," she added.

The campaign includes a dedicated online platform featuring information about all 13 national parks, visitor recommendations, and links to each park's official website. It was developed by creative agency Pastel for the Conservation Carpathia Foundation and the Ministry of Environment, with support from the Romanian Rangers Association.

The Conservation Carpathia Foundation is one of Europe's largest private nature conservation initiatives, working to restore ecosystems in Romania's Southern Carpathian Mountains. Since its establishment in 2009, the foundation has acquired more than 28,000 hectares of forests and alpine meadows for conservation, planted over 4.5 million trees on nearly 2,000 hectares of degraded land, and created a 78,000-hectare no-hunting zone.

Its long-term goal is to support the creation of the Făgăraș Mountains National Park, while promoting biodiversity conservation alongside sustainable economic development for local communities.
