World.title: Three drones target northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Three drones targeted the cities of Sulaimaniyah and Erbil in the Kurdistan region of Iraq early on Sunday before they were shot down without causing any casualties.

According to reports, two drones entered the skies over Sulaimaniyah. One of the two drones resulted in a fire that was eventually extinguished.

In Erbil, the C-RAM air defense system destroyed a drone early this morning without causing any damage.

These strikes follow the unexpected 72-hour pullout of US, British, French, and German forces from Erbil International Airport, which included hundreds of troops and heavy air defense equipment.

US forces have begun a phased withdrawal from Iraqi Kurdistan as part of a plan to redeploy and end their military presence in the country.

Reports indicate that US military convoys have departed from Erbil in the past few days, heading toward neighboring countries.

The US Department of War has not yet issued an official statement regarding the details of these recent movements.

The international coalition’s air defense systems in Erbil intercepted several earlier drones targeting the US consulate and its associated logistics base.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: Iraq forms security committee to prevent attacks against neighboring states
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, chaired an emergency meeting on Saturday to discuss security developments in the region.

Al-Zaidi emphasized the need to prevent any violation or threat emerging from Iraqi land toward neighboring nations, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister directed the establishment of a joint security committee to address current challenges and to follow deterrent procedures to prevent attacks or potential violations against neighboring countries.

Al-Zaidi also directed Iraqi security forces to enhance stability, protect sovereignty, and maintain good neighborly relations.

The meeting addressed the Iraqi army’s readiness to counter any attempt to strike neighboring nations, as well as Iraq’s unwavering commitment to prevent the use of its territory to launch attacks against other countries.

The formation of a joint security committee is part of Iraq’s responsibility to preserve national sovereignty and uphold the principles of good neighborliness and international law.

The decision to form this committee follows substantial regional triggering events in recent days.

The United States and Saudi Arabia launched coordinated attacks on targets in several Iraqi provinces. The alliance declared that these were retaliation strikes in response to drone and missile assaults on regional oil infrastructure and military targets.

Prior to the security meeting, Jordan and Syria cautioned Baghdad about Iran-backed armed groups operating in Iraq, warning that cross-border threats would not go unnoticed.

World.title: Iraqi court recovers IQD 20 billion in corruption and money laundering cases
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq’s Rusafa Investigative Court, which specializes in integrity and money laundering cases, has recovered 20 billion Iraqi dinars (approximately $15.3 million) linked to financial corruption, administrative misconduct, and fraud, the country’s judiciary announced on Sunday.

In a statement, the judiciary’s media office said the recovered funds were tied to investigations involving financial and administrative corruption as well as financial fraud.

The court said the recovery forms part of ongoing legal efforts to pursue individuals accused of using illegal methods to obtain profits at the expense of public funds.

Authorities stressed that legal proceedings against those involved remain underway, reaffirming their commitment to combating corruption and protecting state resources.

The judiciary did not disclose additional details regarding the individuals or entities involved, nor did it specify when the alleged offenses occurred.

World.title: US Embassy in Iraq urges Americans to leave the Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The US Embassy in Baghdad and the US Consulate General in Erbil advised American citizens on Saturday to leave the Middle East as tensions in the region remained high.

The US mission said in a statement that due to heightened tensions in the Middle East, the security environment remains complex with the potential for unforeseen escalation.

The mission added that Americans presently in the Middle East should exercise extreme caution and alertness and be prepared for flight cancellations, frequent airspace closures, and possible travel difficulties.

Some regional airlines have postponed the restart of previously scheduled flights, while others have cancelled some routes.

Americans in the region are advised to consider departing or to be ready to leave if tensions escalate.

In a statement, the US Embassy in Baghdad advised that those who choose to travel to or from the region should closely monitor updates regarding airport and airline operations.

US diplomatic installations, especially those outside the Middle East, have been attacked. Iran and pro-Iran groups may attack additional US interests abroad or at areas connected with the US and Americans across the world, such as US corporations and institutions, according to the statement.

The Iranian leadership is unpredictable, as seen by recent moves to strike regions without notice, as well as to expand assaults to previously untargeted territories such as Egypt, according to the US Embassy in Iraq.

The US Embassy advised Americans to remain vigilant, as the absence of past attacks on US interests or businesses in a country does not ensure their safety.

World.title: Iraq, NATO agree to open mission office in Baghdad, expand security cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews,com) — Iraqi National Security Adviser Qasim al-Aboudi and the commander of the NATO Mission Iraq (NMI), Lt. Gen. Ramon Armada, agreed on Sunday to open a NATO mission office in Baghdad while reaffirming continued cooperation on military training, cybersecurity, and strategic security partnerships.

According to a statement from al-Aboudi’s media office, cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the two officials held talks via video conference to discuss regional security developments and NATO’s ongoing support for Iraq’s armed forces.

During the discussion, both sides stressed the importance of reducing regional tensions and resolving recurring crises through dialogue and diplomatic channels. They also reviewed mechanisms for continuing NATO assistance in the areas of military training, advisory support, intelligence sharing, and capacity building.

A key outcome of the meeting was an agreement to establish a NATO Mission office in Baghdad, further strengthening coordination between the alliance and Iraqi security institutions.

Al-Aboudi said NATO’s role in Iraq remains focused on non-combat activities, including military advisory services, training, capacity building, cybersecurity support, and cooperation in artificial intelligence. He added that Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s government is pursuing a policy of engagement with friendly and neighboring countries to advance development, investment, and mutually beneficial partnerships.

For his part, Armada reaffirmed that NATO’s advisory and training mission is committed to helping develop the capabilities of Iraq’s armed forces to address future security challenges. He said the alliance remains committed to supporting Iraq in line with the priorities established by the Iraqi government.

World.title: Zaidi threatens to resign as Coordination Framework divided over response to Saudi strikes
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi reportedly threatened to resign during a recent meeting of the Coordination Framework amid deep divisions over how Iraq should respond to recent Saudi military strikes, according to a report published Sunday by Baghdad-based newspaper Al-Mada.

Citing political sources, the newspaper said the prime minister’s remarks came during a tense meeting that exposed growing disagreements among senior Shiite leaders over security policy, the role of armed factions, and Baghdad’s handling of escalating regional tensions.

According to the report, the meeting became increasingly heated after intelligence was presented alleging that the armed group Saraya Awliya al-Dam was preparing to launch an attack against Jordan from Iraqi territory. The sources said Amman had warned Baghdad it would respond to any attack originating from Iraq, further intensifying the debate.

The report claims the dispute centered on whether Iraq should adhere to the government’s official position or allow individual armed factions to respond independently to the recent Saudi strikes. While most Coordination Framework leaders reportedly backed the government’s approach, one influential figure with ties to Saraya Awliya al-Dam insisted on carrying out a unilateral response.

Al-Mada reported that armed factions have given the government until next Friday to respond to Saudi Arabia. According to the sources, they warned that if Baghdad fails to act, they may launch their own response.

The newspaper also reported that the escalating dispute prompted al-Zaidi to again raise the possibility of resigning, marking what would be the second time he has reportedly made such a threat since taking office. According to the report, he previously suggested stepping down if his anti-corruption agenda failed.

The sources further claimed that the prime minister is facing mounting political pressure, including concerns about his personal security, although no official statements have confirmed those assertions.

The report also focused on the investigation into drone attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, stating that seven Iraqi-Saudi security meetings, with U.S. participation in some sessions, have been held over the past two months.

According to Al-Mada’s sources, the investigations have not produced conclusive evidence proving that the attacks originated from Iraqi territory, despite Saudi accusations.

The report said several scenarios remain under discussion, including the possibility that Iraqi armed factions were responsible, that Houthi operatives present in Iraq facilitated the attacks, or alternative theories promoted by some factions alleging Israeli activity in Iraq’s southern desert regions.

According to the newspaper, the ongoing crisis led al-Zaidi to cancel a planned visit to Saudi Arabia, which Iraqi officials reportedly viewed as an opportunity to attract much-needed Saudi investment at a time when Iraq faces mounting financial pressures.

The report also said armed factions have urged the prime minister to suspend efforts to bring all weapons under state control, arguing that the recent Saudi strikes have fundamentally altered the security landscape.

Al-Mada also reported that discussions during the meeting touched on the role of Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Chairman Faleh al-Fayyadh during the recent U.S.-Saudi strikes that targeted PMF facilities.

According to the newspaper’s sources, claims circulated that al-Zaidi had warned al-Fayyadh upon returning from Turkey that PMF sites could be targeted, and that evacuation efforts were delayed. However, other participants reportedly dismissed those claims, suggesting they reflected internal political disputes rather than established facts.

The Iraqi government has previously denied having prior knowledge of the U.S.-Saudi strikes. Government spokesman Haider al-Aboudi said Baghdad neither approved nor was informed in advance of the attacks.

However, U.S. President Donald Trump later told Fox News that the strikes had been coordinated with the Iraqi government, presenting an account that differs from Baghdad’s official position.

World.title: Zaidi’s failed raid on Nujaba base exposes challenges in disarmament push
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A failed security operation targeting a facility belonging to the Iran-aligned Harakat al-Nujaba movement has underscored the challenges facing the Iraqi government as it seeks to bring all armed groups under state control before the end of September.

According to a report published by Al-Monitor, a joint Iraqi force attempted to search a Harakat al-Nujaba compound in Baghdad’s Jurf al-Naddaf district on July 24 after receiving intelligence suggesting the site contained missiles and drones. However, the operation ended without the facility being searched after armed members of the group confronted government forces.

The report, citing Iraqi security officials, said the operation involved Baghdad Operations Command, the Federal Police, and the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) Security Directorate. Shortly after arriving at the compound, commanders affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba reportedly ordered their fighters to prevent security personnel from entering. Armed members of the group then surrounded the government force and fired warning shots into the air, forcing the operation to halt.

According to the officials, the PMF leadership subsequently instructed its personnel to withdraw, stating they had not been informed that the target was a facility affiliated with Harakat al-Nujaba. Army units involved in the operation later received similar withdrawal orders. No casualties were reported, and neither the government nor the armed group publicly disclosed details of the incident at the time.

The incident comes as Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has pledged to ensure that all weapons in Iraq are brought under state control by September 30, the scheduled end of the U.S.-led coalition’s military mission in the country.

Al-Monitor described the failed operation as the first significant field test of the government’s commitment to enforcing that pledge. While previous administrations also announced plans to limit weapons to state institutions, implementation has remained difficult due to the political and military influence of several armed factions.

Hayder al-Shakeri, a researcher with Chatham House’s Middle East and North Africa Programme, told Al-Monitor that although Baghdad has increasingly relied on restructuring security institutions and applying political and financial pressure on armed groups, the Jurf al-Naddaf operation demonstrated the limits of the state’s authority when confronted directly.

“If the government cannot enforce its decisions against a single armed faction, or fails to follow through with legal and political accountability, it suggests that these groups still retain an effective veto over certain state actions,” Al-Shakeri was quoted as saying.

The report noted that not all Iran-aligned factions share the same position regarding government efforts to centralize weapons under state control.

Some groups, including Asaib Ahl al-Haq, have become increasingly integrated into Iraq’s political and economic systems, potentially reducing their willingness to engage in direct confrontation. Others—including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada—continue to oppose any move that would place their military capabilities under full government authority.

Political analyst Muhannad al-Ghazi told Al-Monitor that these factions view their weapons through an ideological lens, making voluntary disarmament highly unlikely. He argued that targeting isolated weapons caches without addressing broader military infrastructure would have only a limited impact.

The reported confrontation occurred amid heightened regional tensions following Prime Minister al-Zaidi’s recent visit to Washington, where Iraq and the United States announced a strategic economic partnership.

According to Al-Monitor, several Iran-backed factions criticized the visit, warning against what they described as replacing “military occupation” with “economic occupation” through expanded U.S. investment in Iraq.

The report also linked the incident to broader regional developments, including recent drone attacks and cross-border military operations that have intensified pressure on Baghdad’s efforts to assert control over its territory.

Al-Monitor concluded that the government’s September 30 target for fully disarming armed factions appears increasingly difficult to achieve given current realities.

Instead, analysts cited by the publication believe Baghdad may focus on more gradual measures, including relocating some weapons, closing selected facilities, and increasing political and financial pressure on groups willing to cooperate, while avoiding direct confrontation with the most heavily armed factions.

The report suggested that the ultimate success of Iraq’s disarmament strategy may depend not only on domestic enforcement but also on broader regional dynamics, particularly relations between the United States and Iran.

World.title: Jordan threatens to strike Iranian militias in Iraq if they launched attacks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Amman has publicly warned Iraq that it will launch military operations against Iran-backed militias if they attack Jordan.

The warning comes after a rapid increase in regional violence, including recent interceptions of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones over Jordanian airspace, which targeted US installations.

An official Jordanian source told Al-Arabiya News that Jordan provided Iraq with precise intelligence indicating that pro-Iran militants are planning to strike Jordanian territory.

Jordan has publicly said that it expects the Iraqi government to take quick and effective measures to curb these armed groups.

Jordanian sources identify front organizations such as Awliya al-Dam as key players in these border-threatening actions.

The warning represents a strong change in Jordan’s defensive stance in the face of rising tensions between the United States and Iran.

Jordan harbors critical Western military installations, such as the Muwaffaq Salti Air Base, which have become active targets for the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) and its allies in the region.

Jordan emphasized that, while it aims to avoid regional escalation, it considers national sovereignty and border security to be inviolable priorities.

World.title: Congress set to stall House over Ram temple donation scam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Signaling continuing disruption in Parliament in the coming week, Congress has accused

and home minister

of avoiding Parliament at a time when the Opposition has been raising the crucial issue of Ayodhya donation scam.

We will take this issue to the public, persist in the fight until the guilty are punished and raise this matter again in the House Monday," Tiwari said.

World.title: DMK slams Congress for 'trading trust for berths'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: DMK Sunday mounted a furious pushback against Rahul Gandhi's describing any support to govt's widely speculated move to revive the bill to increase Lok Sabha's strength, coupled with delimitation of constituencies, as a betrayal of Tamil Nadu amid buzz in political circles that the regional party may come around to backing the measure.

A day after Rahul, during his visit to Tamil Nadu, said any party supporting the constitution amendment bill in Parliament will be a 21st century Ettappan, a historical figure reviled for treachery, senior DMK MP Dayanidhi Maran came out with a blistering retort. "These are the people who traded our trust in them for mere ministerial berths," he said, lashing out at "poisonous snakes" which sell trust to "buy" power, a reference to Congress's decision to snap ties with DMK and TVK.

Maran's strongly worded rejoinder captured the lingering sense of betrayal within the Dravidian party over Congress's swift embrace of its rival after the national party went to the poll as DMK's ally and was fully backed by the latter on all key issues, including Rahul's leadership, in national politics through its years in office.

BJP is hopeful that DMK's bubbling anger with Congress will help its bid to win over the party's support for its key legislative measures, especially delimitation, in Parliament, even though govt has so far not taken any official step to revive the bill that was defeated by a united Opposition in the last session.





DMK has anyway indicated its openness over the issue, saying it will take a call after studying the bill and insisting that the proposed law should not harm south India's interests.

Rahul's comments are also a nod to the acknowledgement in Opposition camp of the possibility of DMK revising its stand on a bill which, opposition parties have alleged, will allow BJP-led governing alliance to reconfigure constituencies to its advantage for the 2029 Lok Sabha poll.

World.title: SC warns Punjab for ignoring 15-yr-old ruling on dues to Himachal Pradesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Punjab govt's stiff resistance to attorney general R Venkataramani's proposal for amicable implementation of a 15-year-old Supreme Court decree settling Bhakra Nangal and Beas power dues since 1966 in favour of Himachal Pradesh made SC observe, "The state has a habit of defying decrees and old habits die hard.

"

Venkataramani told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that he had extensive consultations with Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Union ministry of power after getting the records examined by CAG for independent determination of the historical capital cost liability.

"...a mutually workable settlement framework has been evolved. It envisages a cashless settlement, wherein the respective claims and liabilities are proposed to be adjusted through in-kind settlement of energy arrears and set-off of capital cost liability, thereby obviating the need for any direct financial transaction between the states," the AG said.

Senior advocates Kapil Sibal and Balbir Singh, appearing for Himachal and Haryana, respectively, said they were agreeable with the AG's settlement proposal for implementation of the decree, which was passed by the SC in 2011 on an original suit filed by Himachal 30 years ago seeking settlement of assets on division of Punjab in 1966.

For Punjab, senior advocate Nidhesh Gupta said the state had key concerns over workability of the AG's proposal and said the state would stand to lose substantially.





Given the fact that it is a 15-year-old decree passed on a 30-year-old original suit seeking resolution of a 60-year-old inter-state dispute, the bench said, "Your state has a habit of defying decrees..."

"There is a decree in Himachal's favour. When we order implement, it will be with interest from 2011. We will not allow them to be deprived of the fruits of the decree. If you settle, it is well and good. Otherwise, be ready for consequences."

It posted the matter for hearing on Aug 12.

In its July 30 order, the bench said, "While the states of Himachal and Haryana have graciously agreed in principle to the proposal, the state of Punjab has raised objections thereto. In the interest of justice, two weeks time is granted to Punjab to reconsider and clarify its stand."

The AG's proposal had said, "Punjab and Haryana will provide 13,066 MU of energy arrears to HP at 871 MU per annum over 15 lean seasons (Oct-March), in the inter-se ratio of 58:42 (Bhakra Nangal project) and 60:40 (Beas projects).

HP to pay BBMB-determined charges for the year in which each tranche is received.

"HP's liability (7.19% of composite Punjab) towards the capital cost of Bhakra Nangal and Beas projects - being the unreimbursed share of loan servicing by Punjab and Haryana since 1966-67 - be assessed at Rs 420.7 crore (Punjab: Rs 249.2 crore; Haryana: Rs 171.5 crore). The capital cost liability could be considered to set off against part of HP's energy arrear receivables.

"

SC on Sept 27, 2011 (Justices R V Raveendran and A K Patnaik) had decreed the suit in favour of HP by ruling, "The state is entitled to 7.19% of the power of the composite state of Punjab from the Bhakra Nangal project with effect from Nov 1, 1966, and from Beas project with effect from the dates of production in Unit I and Unit II."

World.title: Ramlila body asks 'Ramayana' makers to hold special screening before release, warns of protests
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Shri Ramlila Mahasangh has asked the makers of Ranbir Kapoor-starrer Ramayana to hold a special preview screening for its representatives before the film's worldwide theatrical release, warning that it will stage protests if the request is not accepted.

In a letter addressed to director Nitesh Tiwari and the film's production company, Shri Ramlila Mahasangh president Arjun Kumar sought a screening of the film ahead of its Diwali 2026 release in India and overseas to ensure it does not contain scenes that could hurt Hindu sentiments.

The demand comes in the backdrop of the controversy surrounding the 2023 film Adipurush, which drew criticism over its depiction of characters and settings from the Hindu epic.

Recalling the earlier controversy, Kumar said members of the Sanatan community and those associated with traditional Ramlila performances had objected to several aspects of Adipurush, including "the depiction of Lanka in black instead of gold, and the portrayal of Ravana and his army in a manner that did not align with traditional beliefs."

"According to information received by the Mahasangh, Ramayana may also contain certain scenes that could hurt the sentiments of Hindus living in India and abroad.





In light of this, the organisation has requested a special preview screening to ensure that any potentially objectionable scenes or dialogues are identified and removed prior to release," Kumar said in a press note.

He also warned that if the filmmakers do not agree to the request, the Shri Ramlila Mahasangh, along with various Hindu organisations, will stage protests and demonstrations outside cinema halls in Delhi and other states.

World.title: Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
World.content:
Franz Kafka's The Metamorphosis transformed an ordinary man into a giant insect to explore alienation, helplessness and the dehumanising pressures of modern life.

More than a century later, India's self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has adopted a similarly unsettling symbol, not to tell a work of fiction, but to express the frustrations of a generation increasingly unsure whether years of education, expensive coaching and relentless competition will ever translate into a stable job.

What began as a social media sensation with a strong and straightforward satirical structure, quickly evolved into one of the country's biggest youth-led movements in recent years.

Calling itself the "voice of the lazy and unemployed," the movement grew from memes mocking joblessness, paper leaks, inflation and the political establishment into street protests.

The protest may have become a trigger for a generation already grappling with shrinking employment opportunities, rising educational costs and growing uncertainty about the future.

And at its heart lies a simple question. What happens when an economy produces millions of graduates every year but fails to create enough quality jobs?

According to veteran economist

, a retired professor at JNU, "This unemployment crisis has created a huge gap between expectations and reality."

"Young people earn degrees believing they will secure good jobs, but when those jobs do not materialise, they continue preparing for competitive examinations year after year. Many take these exams four, five or even six times because they still hope to secure an organised sector job.





Their parents also encourage them because they know such jobs offer stable salaries and social security," he said.

"But the increasing privatisation of education has intensified competition. Coaching institutes want to showcase high success rates because that is their biggest selling point. That creates incentives for unethical practices, including paper leaks. The greater the privatisation, the greater the pressure to resort to illegal methods to ensure students succeed.

Fake degrees, cheating and question paper leaks are all symptoms of a much deeper problem.

They are linked to unemployment and the shortage of quality jobs in the organised sector," he added.

India's employment challenge



India has spent decades expanding access to higher education. Universities have multiplied, enrollment has surged and millions of families have invested heavily in degrees, viewing education as the surest path to upward mobility.

The numbers tell a remarkable story. According to the State of Working India 2026 report by Azim Premji University, the number of young graduates in India increased nearly 13-fold, rising from around 5 million in 1983 to 63 million in 2023.

But while the supply of graduates has grown rapidly, employment opportunities have not kept pace.

The report estimates that graduate unemployment among people below the age of 25 is now close to 40%, while graduates accounted for nearly two-thirds of India's unemployed population in 2023.

Even more striking is the rise in the number of unemployed graduates, which has increased from less than one million in 1983 to around 11 million in 2023, a 16-fold increase over four decades.

The mismatch between education and employment has widened steadily since the mid-2000s as higher education expanded much faster than the creation of quality jobs. For millions of families, earning a college degree no longer guarantees stable employment or financial security.

Recent government data suggest that the challenge is becoming even more severe.

According to the government's flagship Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), unemployment among Indians aged 15 to 29 rose to 16.2% in June, the highest level recorded since monthly estimates became available in April 2025. At that time, youth unemployment stood at 13.8%.

The ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI) has cautioned that monthly figures may fluctuate because of seasonal factors, academic cycles and the increased frequency of surveys.

Even so, the latest numbers are significant because they fit into a broader pattern rather than representing an isolated spike. Youth unemployment has increased across all six categories tracked by the survey, urban and rural areas, men and women alike, during the 15 months for which monthly data are available.

At the same time, the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) among young people has declined from 42.7% to 40.3%.

In simple terms, fewer young people are actively looking for work.

Ordinarily, such a decline would be expected to reduce unemployment because fewer people are participating in the labour market. Instead, unemployment has continued to rise, suggesting that the economy is not generating enough opportunities even for the shrinking pool of job seekers.

Annual PLFS data reinforce the same trend. Between 2022 and 2025, youth unemployment increased in 13 states and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Telangana and West Bengal.

The situation appears even more challenging for young women, with unemployment rising across 16 states and Union Territories during the same period.

Taken together, the figures suggest that youth unemployment is becoming a structural challenge rather than a temporary fluctuation.

The problem isn't just unemployment, it's job quality



Headline unemployment figures often fail to capture the deeper challenges within India's labour market. Many graduates do find work, but not necessarily the kind of work they expected after spending years in higher education.

Economist Arun Kumar said that the root of the problem is the sharp divide between India's organised and unorganised sectors.

"When unemployment rises, it inevitably leads to greater conflict because there are too few jobs for too many people. In India, this problem is even more pronounced because the unorganised sector employs around 94% of the workforce, while the organised sector employs only about 6%. The difference in wages and job security between these two sectors is enormous.

A courier delivery worker may earn around Rs 10,000-12,000 a month, whereas a postman can earn around Rs 70,000.

Naturally, nobody wants to lose an organised sector job, and everyone wants to secure one. That intense competition creates immense pressure," he added.

An analysis of India's Periodic Labour Force Survey illustrates this disconnect. Out of every 100 graduates aged between 15 and 29, only 50 are employed, 15 remain unemployed while actively searching for work, and the remaining 35 are outside the labour force altogether.

Some continue their education. Others perform unpaid domestic work or have simply stopped looking for employment after repeated disappointments.

Even among those who are employed, the quality of jobs remains a major concern. Only 26 out of every 100 graduates have regular salaried jobs. More strikingly, just four hold formal jobs that provide written contracts, paid leave and social security benefits.

The remaining graduates are spread across self-employment, unpaid family work, casual labour and small household enterprises.

Many earn irregular incomes and lack job security despite years spent pursuing higher education.

The figures highlight a growing reality in India's labour market: employment alone is no longer an adequate measure of economic well-being. The challenge is increasingly about the availability of secure, productive and reasonably paid jobs.

Why educated youth feel left behind

The employment crisis begins long before students enter the labour market.

Competition for limited seats in prestigious colleges has transformed education itself into an expensive investment.

Government survey data show that Indian households now spend a significantly larger share of their education budgets on private coaching than they did seven years ago.

The sharpest increase has been among higher secondary students preparing for engineering, medical and university entrance examinations.

Families now spend nearly one-fourth of their higher secondary education budgets on coaching, compared with about 18% in 2018.

Private coaching expenses have also increased steadily across primary, middle and secondary education, reflecting a growing belief that classroom teaching alone is no longer sufficient to compete in high-stakes entrance examinations.

The pressure becomes particularly visible in engineering education.

India had around 4.4 million undergraduate engineering students during the 2023-24 academic year. Yet the country's top 100 engineering institutions together offered only about 500,000 seats.

In effect, only one in nine engineering students can study at an institution widely regarded as offering strong placements and better career prospects.

Students who fail to secure admission to elite institutions often graduate from colleges with weaker placement records, making it significantly harder to obtain well-paying jobs.

The widening gap between educational aspirations and employment outcomes has created growing frustration among young people. The traditional promise that more education automatically leads to better employment is becoming increasingly uncertain.

According to the State of Working India 2026 report, fewer than 7% of male graduates secure a permanent salaried job within one year of graduating. The figure is even lower, just 3.7%, when it comes to white-collar jobs.

Using data from the PLFS and the earlier Employment-Unemployment Survey, the report estimates that 1.1 crore out of India's 6.3 crore graduates aged between 20 and 29 were unemployed in 2023.

Graduate unemployment itself is not a new phenomenon. The report estimates that unemployment among graduates below the age of 25 increased from 35.02% in 1983 to 39.33% in 2023.

What has changed, however, is the scale of the problem. India now produces far more graduates than ever before, while simultaneously entering the most important phase of its demographic transition.

The country's median age currently stands at around 29 years and is expected to rise to 38 years by 2050.

This is the period during which India's working-age population is expected to drive economic growth. If the economy fails to generate enough productive employment during this demographic window, the much-discussed demographic dividend could gradually turn into a demographic challenge.

India's employment paradox



India today is one of the world's fastest-growing major economies.

Even amid geopolitical tensions, volatile oil prices and slowing global trade, the country has continued to post robust GDP growth and position itself as a manufacturing and investment hub.

The government has invested heavily in highways, airports, railways, ports and digital infrastructure. Global technology companies such as Apple have expanded manufacturing in India, electronics exports have surged and semiconductor investments are beginning to gather pace.

Policymakers increasingly see manufacturing as the sector that can absorb millions of workers and turn India's demographic advantage into sustained economic growth.

Yet for many young Indians entering the labour market, this optimism feels distant. The central contradiction facing the Indian economy is that rapid economic growth has not translated into an equivalent expansion in quality employment.

Economists often describe this phenomenon as "jobless growth", an economy that continues to grow without creating enough secure and productive jobs.

India's challenge is especially daunting because nearly eight million graduates enter the labour market every year. Generating employment for such a large number of educated young people has become one of the country's biggest economic challenges.

This gap between economic growth and employment opportunities lies at the heart of the frustration that has fuelled recent youth protests.

Is India creating enough jobs?



Whether India is creating enough jobs depends largely on which dataset is examined.

The Reserve Bank of India's KLEMS database estimated that the economy generated 4.7 crore jobs during 2023-24, the highest annual increase in more than four decades.

However, labour economists caution against looking at headline employment numbers alone.

Employment estimates differ across official surveys because they use different methodologies. More importantly, the definition of employment itself often masks the underlying quality of jobs being created.

For instance, India's labour surveys classify a person as employed if they have worked even for a few days during the reference period.

Likewise, unpaid family workers and subsistence self-employed individuals are counted as employed despite earning little or no regular income.

As a result, headline employment figures may paint a healthier picture than what many young workers experience in reality. Increasingly, economists argue that the more important question is no longer how many jobs India is creating, but what kind of jobs they are.

The informal sector is slowing too



For decades, India's informal economy acted as a safety valve for the labour market. Workers unable to secure formal employment often found opportunities in small businesses, family enterprises, retail trade or self-employment.

However, even this safety net appears to be weakening.

According to the ministry of statistics and programme implementation's latest Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE), the informal sector generated around 74.5 lakh jobs in 2025, significantly lower than the 1.1 crore jobs created during the previous survey period ending September 2024.

Wage growth has also slowed sharply. Average wage growth in the sector declined to 3.9%, compared with 13% previously, suggesting that even workers who manage to find employment are seeing slower improvements in earnings.

The figures reinforce concerns that employment opportunities are weakening across both formal and informal sectors, making it increasingly difficult for young people to find stable livelihoods.

India's employment quality lags behind peers



India's labour market also differs from many comparable economies because of the quality of employment available.

International comparisons reveal another structural weakness: the quality of employment. Labour market studies show that around 93% of employed workers in Russia hold regular jobs. The share is about 68% in Brazil, 54% in China and 42% in Bangladesh, the PLFS 2022-23 & Jan-Mar 2024 data reported.

In India, by contrast, only about 23% of workers are in regular salaried employment.

This means that nearly three-fourths of Indian workers remain outside the formal sector, without written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or social security.

The shortage of secure employment also explains the extraordinary demand for government jobs. Whether it is railways, banking, the armed forces, civil services or state recruitment

examinations, millions of candidates compete for relatively few vacancies because government employment still offers something much of the private sector cannot consistently provide stability.

A government job often brings predictable salaries, pensions, housing allowances, healthcare benefits and long-term security.

For many young Indians, particularly those from middle- and lower-income households, these jobs represent far more than employment. They represent financial stability for entire families.

According to Kumar, the desperation is visible in the jobs educated Indians are willing to apply for.

The real issue is the lack of decent employment opportunities. We saw this clearly in Uttar Pradesh in 2017, when more than two lakh people applied for peon posts. Many applicants held qualifications such as PhDs, MTech, BTech, MCom and BCom degrees. When highly educated people apply for peon jobs, it shows they are unable to find work that matches their qualifications. Arun Kumar

AI adds a new challenge



Even as India grapples with creating quality jobs, technological change is reshaping the employment landscape.

A government-backed research group estimates that artificial intelligence could displace around three million managerial and coding jobs by the end of this decade.

Automation is expected to reduce demand for routine white-collar work at a time when India is producing record numbers of engineering and technology graduates.

Overseas opportunities are also becoming more limited. Tighter immigration policies in countries such as the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia have reduced opportunities for skilled Indian professionals.

For decades, migration acted as a safety valve for India's educated workforce. That pathway is becoming increasingly uncertain.

"Many young Indians even leave the country in search of better opportunities.

Some spend lakhs of rupees to migrate, while others take illegal routes because they see very few prospects at home. In many cases, they still end up doing low-paying or menial jobs abroad. That reflects the level of desperation created by the lack of opportunities in India,"Kumar noted on the brain-drain situation in India.

India's demographic dividend at a crossroads



India possesses one of the world's youngest populations, a demographic advantage that economists have long viewed as one of the country's greatest strengths.

A growing working-age population has the potential to accelerate economic growth, boost productivity and expand domestic consumption.

But demographic dividends are never automatic. They depend on whether an economy can generate enough productive employment for the millions entering the labour market every year.

Research suggests that India's employment intensity of growth, the ability of economic expansion to generate jobs has steadily declined over the past four decades.

When NEET became the tipping point



Against this backdrop, the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak became much more than an examination controversy. Millions of students spend months and often years preparing for the country's most competitive entrance examinations.

Families invest heavily in coaching classes, relocate to education hubs and, in many cases, students take gap years in pursuit of a medical seat.

When allegations emerged that the examination paper had been leaked and sold before the test, the issue struck at the heart of a system that already demanded enormous financial and emotional investment.

The government cancelled the examination, handed the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation and ordered a re-examination.

For lakhs of aspirants, particularly those from middle- and lower-income households, the cancellation meant far more than repeating a test. It meant another year of uncertainty after months of preparation and considerable financial sacrifice.

Some students performed worse in the re-examination. Others worried they had lost their best chance of securing admission.

Reports of severe psychological stress and alleged student suicides linked to the controversy further intensified public anger.

What began as protests against examination irregularities gradually evolved into a wider movement about education, unemployment and shrinking opportunities.

It was in this atmosphere that the Cockroach Janta Party found resonance among young Indians. Initially known for satirical social media posts, the movement soon expanded into organised protests questioning paper leaks, unemployment, inflation and what participants described as the growing disconnect between educational aspirations and employment opportunities.

The group's unusual symbol, the cockroach, captured widespread attention.

The insect represented resilience, survival and invisibility, mirroring how many young people felt overlooked despite years of education and preparation. Eventually, the protests became one of the biggest youth movements witnessed in recent years.

The protests exposed far more than frustration over one examination. They revealed a widening disconnect between education, employment and economic expectations.

Economist Arun Kumar says unemployment extends far beyond those who are officially counted as jobless.

"Youth unemployment, particularly among those aged 15 to 29, is extremely high, and the situation is especially difficult for women. There are different forms of unemployment. First, there are those actively looking for work but unable to find it. Second, there are people who are technically employed but only in low-paid, part-time or menial jobs that do not provide a decent livelihood," he said.

"Third, there is disguised unemployment, where people appear to be working but contribute little to productive economic activity. Finally, there are those who have stopped looking for work altogether because they have lost hope. Women are disproportionately represented in this last category. Female labour force participation in India remains much lower than in many other major economies, which means many women are no longer even counted among active job seekers," he added.

Over the past few decades, India has dramatically expanded access to higher education, produced record numbers of graduates and remained one of the world's fastest-growing major economies.

But the growth in quality jobs has failed to keep pace with the growing pool of educated youth. For many young Indians, securing a degree no longer guarantees a stable career or upward social mobility.

That gap between aspirations and opportunities lies at the heart of the growing frustration.

For millions of students, the question is no longer just whether examinations are conducted fairly.

It is whether years of education, expensive coaching, repeated attempts at competitive exams and immense financial sacrifices will eventually lead to a secure, well-paying job. Without that, the frustrations exposed by such protests are likely to persist long after the headlines fade.

World.title: BMC to monitor illegal waste dumping through CCTV surveillance
World.content:
The Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) launched a citywide cleanliness drive following Bombay High Court’s directions, with civic authorities deciding to install CCTV cameras at garbage dumping hotspots and impose strict penalties on those found littering or illegally dumping waste.

The corporation’s Solid Waste Management Department launched the comprehensive campaign to improve visible cleanliness across Mumbai and its suburbs, prevent open dumping and permanently eliminate Garbage Vulnerable Points (GVPs), where garbage is repeatedly dumped.

Municipal Commissioner Ashwini Bhide on August 1 directed Assistant Commissioners of all ward offices to conduct regular inspections and ensure high standards of sanitation in their respective jurisdictions.

The drive is intended to ensure that all identified GVPs will be monitored through CCTV cameras, and illegal garbage dumping will be penalised. The points have been identified and mapped ward-wise on Google Maps and will be studied for type of garbage and shortcomings in waste management.

The civic body also launched a drive to make Mumbai’s footpaths obstruction-free. with Assistant Commissioners instructed to remove encroachments from footpaths along major roads to keep unauthorised hawkers and illegal ramps away.

Further, the BMC directed officials to address traffic bottlenecks on major roads and prioritise to pothole complaints received on the Marg App. BMC is also set to take immediate action against unauthorised constructions across Mumbai

World.title: Students continue protests in Ranchi over alleged JPSC, JSSC exam irregularities, demand CBI probe
World.content:
Hundreds of students continued their protest for the fifth consecutive day in Ranchi on Sunday (August 2, 2026) over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests, demanding a CBI probe and reforms in the recruitment agencies.

The protesters, who have been holding an indefinite sit-in at a stadium since July 29, raised slogans such as 'Order CBI probe in JPSC', 'Long live Students Unity' and 'Shame on Hemant Soren'.

"Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied," JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said.

He alleged that previous probes into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission (JSSC)-CGL paper leak had not led to action and claimed that the latest investigation could also be "covered up" after a few months.

"We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister's resignation on moral grounds," Mr. Kranti said.

The protesters are demanding cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19 and an independent probe by central agencies, including the CBI and Enforcement Directorate (ED), into alleged irregularities in recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC.

They are also demanding the introduction of a fifth option of "not attempted" in OMR sheets.

"The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers' families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit," said Ankit Kumar from Giridih district.

Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.

"I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands," she said.

Archana Kumari from Palamu said the protesters would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities.

"The State government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest," said Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district.

Meanwhile, thousands of students held a torchlight procession in the state capital this evening.

The students, who are holding an indefinite sit-in at the Jaipal Singh Munda stadium, marched to Albert Ekka Chowk. There, they raised slogans against the JMM-led alliance government and demanded an impartial probe into the alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC, JSCC-CGL and other state-level public recruitment tests.

They said if the state government does not address their concerns, they will march to the Jharkhand Assembly and stage a gherao in the next couple of days.

"We have been holding protests, but no government officials approached us to listen to our concerns on these issues. This clearly shows the insensitivity of this JMM-led alliance government towards the thousands of students and youths of the state," they alleged.

World.title: Moscow Mayor calls deadly bomb attack on a restaurant a 'terrorist act'
World.content:
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin called on Sunday (August 2, 2026) a bomb attack on a restaurant in the capital the day before a “brutal terrorist act,” but did not say who was responsible.

The blast on Saturday (August 1) evening at the Balzi Rossi, an upscale Italian establishment in central Moscow, killed three people, including the woman bomber, Russian state media said, citing local officials.

“Yesterday, a brutal terrorist act was committed in Moscow that claimed human lives. The victims are currently in the city's hospitals, where they are receiving all necessary care,” Mr. Sobyanin wrote on social media on Sunday (August 2).

He added that a probe into the attack was underway. “Those responsible for committing this crime will certainly be found and will face the punishment they deserve,” he wrote.

At least 21 people were wounded when the explosive device detonated at the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square, the National Anti-Terrorism Committee said late on Saturday (August 1), according to Russian state news agency Ria Novosti.

A woman attempted to smuggle the bomb into the establishment, but a security guard refused to let her in before the bomb exploded, reported Ria Novosti. The Moscow Investigative Committee said on Saturday evening the attack was still being investigated.

As of early afternoon on Sunday (August 2), there was no further information from Russian authorities, and no one had publicly claimed responsibility.

According to Ria Novosti, the restaurant was closed for a private function on Saturday (August 1) evening.

Footage released by Russian state media showed heavily armed law-enforcement officers, several ambulances and other emergency vehicles at the site.

Earlier this year, Russia's Federal Security Service announced that authorities would tighten security around senior military and government officials, after a series of assassination attempts in Russian cities that followed the Kremlin's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

So far, Russian authorities have not drawn any connections between Saturday's (August 2) blast and these earlier attacks or the war in Ukraine.

Russia previously said Kyiv was behind a car bombing in Moscow last April that killed Lt Gen Yaroslav Moskalik, a deputy head of the main operational department in Russia's General Staff. Ukraine did not publicly claim responsibility.

But Ukraine's SBU security service earlier said it had organized the killing in December 2024 of Lt Gen Igor Kirillov, who headed the Russian military's nuclear, biological and chemical protection forces.

Kirillov was killed by a bomb hidden in a scooter outside his apartment building in Moscow, a day after Ukraine's security service leveled criminal charges against him.

Among other prominent victims of bombing attacks in Russia were Daria Dugina, the daughter of influential nationalist thinker Aleksandr Dugin, and Vladlen Tatarsky, a well-known pro-Kremlin military blogger.

Kyiv denied involvement in the attack on Dugina, and did not respond to Russian accusations that it was behind Tatarsky's death.

World.title: 1.35 lakh affected still affected by floods in Assam; 3 more deaths take toll to 85
World.content:
The flood situation in Assam improved on Sunday (August 2, 2026) with around 1.35 lakh people now affected in five districts even though three more persons died, taking the toll in this year's deluge to 85, according to an official bulletin.

All three deaths were reported from Sivasagar district.

The Assam State Disaster Management Authority (ASDMA) reported that more than 1,36,200 people have been affected by floods in the Charaideo, Dhemaji, Golaghat, Jorhat, and Sivasagar districts. On Saturday (August 1), almost 1.8 lakh people were affected across five districts.

Sivasagar is the worst-hit district with over 55,000 people affected, followed by 40,000 people in Charaideo and 22,000 in Jorhat. According to ASDMA, 335 villages are inundated, while 15,422 hectares of farmland have been damaged.

The administration has been operating 54 relief camps and relief distribution centres in five districts, taking care of 13,771 people at present.

At present, the Dhansiri river is flowing above the danger level at Numaligarh.

World.title: 75-year-old digital arrest victim moves HC for CBI probe; Delhi Police asked to file status report
World.content:
Vibha*, a 75-year-old breast cancer survivor who was forced to sell her home in south Delhi’s Vasant Kunj, pawn her gold jewellery and part with nearly ₹3 lakh in a digital arrest scam, has moved the Delhi High Court seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe, alleging that the Delhi police have made “little meaningful progress” since the FIR was registered in April this year.

On July 30, Ms. Vibha and her daughter, Seema Chauhan*, filed a writ petition in the High Court seeking the transfer of the case to the Central probe agency. The court has issued notices to the police and the CBI seeking their response. It has also asked the police to submit a detailed status report within two weeks and posted the matter for hearing on August 13.

“This is a case where the fraudsters not only forced an elderly woman to be under continuous video surveillance but also showed up at her doorstep, thereby involving digital as well as physical extortion and harassment. This is why we have sought a CBI inquiry into the case,” said Kush Sharma, the advocate representing the two petitioners.

‘Worst crime’

The plea also cited the Supreme Court’s directions from December 1, 2025, in a suo motu case in which the court observed that senior citizens are the most targeted victims in digital arrest cases and that the CBI must be the primary agency to investigate such cases.

The apex court has repeatedly expressed concern over such cases. Last week, a three-judge Bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant said, “Digital arrest scams are the worst kind of crime against people, especially senior citizens whose life savings and hard-earned money are fraudulently siphoned out when they need it the most.”

Month-long ordeal

Ms. Vibha was under digital arrest from April 6 to 27. Men claiming to be from the CBI told her to hand over her savings, jewellery and property in order to avoid action from the Enforcement Directorate, threatening to bring her children, who live outside India, back to the country and arrest them if she did not comply.

Her daughter, who lives in the Netherlands, returned to India as soon as she found out about the crime, after which an FIR was registered on April 27.

Since then, the senior citizen said, the police have not updated them on the investigation, even as the family continues to receive phone calls and messages from the perpetrators.

“The fraudsters are still at large and have been harassing my mother by calling her multiple times and sending messages and e-mails,” said Ms. Chauhan.

“When I contacted the investigating officer and told him that my mother is still getting calls and messages from them, he told me he would summon them for interrogation after I returned to India. All this while, the police did not take any action against them,” she claimed.

When reached for comment, investigating officer Subhash Pokhriyal said the police have identified multiple bank account holders to whom the proceeds from the crime were transferred.

“At least 10-12 bank accounts have been identified. We are interrogating the account holders,” he said.

(*Names changed on request)

World.title: Congress hits out at Delhi government’s water ATM plan
World.content:
The Delhi Congress on Sunday accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government of failing to provide piped water to every household and criticised its plan to install water ATMs in areas without pipeline connectivity.

Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav said the proposal did not address the problem and was an attempt to divert attention from the government’s failure to expand the pipeline network. He demanded a time-bound expansion of the water pipeline network, a permanent water supply instead of temporary measures like tankers and water ATMs, and a public action plan with timelines for water-scarce areas.

“Instead of providing a modern water supply system to the Capital, the BJP government is implementing a system that forces people to queue up to collect water. Grand promises were made ahead of the election to provide piped connections and clean drinking water to every household, yet the government itself now admits that many areas of Delhi still lack pipeline connectivity,” he said.

Mr. Yadav said the proposed ₹58-crore expenditure on 250 water ATMs showed that the government had failed to provide a permanent solution.

He said the money could instead have been used to expand the water pipeline network, plug leaks and strengthen the distribution system, which would have provided lasting relief to lakhs of people.

World.title: M.K. Sanoo never saw continuous LDF rule as dangerous, says Pinarayi Vijayan
World.content:
Professor M.K. Sanoo had never believed that continuous rule by a political front was dangerous, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan said here on Sunday (August 2, 2026) in a veiled attack on cultural figures who had warned against the Left Democratic Front (LDF) retaining power in the State. He added that Prof. Sanoo was someone who never attempted to enhance his image by tarnishing the Left front.

He was inaugurating a commemorative meeting marking the first death anniversary of the renowned Malayalam literary critic, orator, and former MLA, organised by the Prof. M.K. Sanoo Master Samskarika Kendram.

“One may receive applause and greater public acceptance if one criticises the Left from within the fold. Sanoo Master was well aware of his position in people’s minds and knew that he did not have to resort to such fake methods to improve his public image. Those who lacked such self-awareness had to adopt other stances,” Mr. Vijayan said.

In what sounded like a veiled criticism of former Kerala Sahitya Akademi president K. Satchidanandan, Mr. Vijayan recalled how gracefully Prof. Sanoo had served in the same position during an earlier tenure of the LDF. Mr. Satchidanandan’s comments cautioning against a prolonged rule by the LDF had sparked a major political controversy ahead of the Assembly elections.

Earlier in the day, Mr. Vijayan presented the maiden ‘Sanoo Sammanam’, instituted by the Samskarika Kendram, to Malayalam literary stalwart M. Leelavathy at her home in Thrikkakara. Receiving the lifetime achievement award, which carries a cash prize of₹1 lakh, a statuette and a certificate, Ms. Leelavathy said she had mixed feelings about the honour. “I’m deeply pained to receive the award instituted in the name of a long-time colleague in his absence. At the same time, I’m glad to receive it as a blessing from him, considering the deep friendship we shared,” she said. Ms. Leelavathy announced that she would donate the cash award to Kanivu Pain and Palliative Care. The Sanoo Sammanam Yuvaprathibha Puraskaram was presented to historian Vinil Paul at the event. Writer N.S. Madhavan chaired the meeting.

CPI(M) leaders P. Rajeeve, C.N. Mohanan, S. Sharma, C.M. Dinesh Mani, S. Sathish and M. Anilkumar, writers Sunil P. Elayidom and Thanooja Bhattathiri and journalist R. Rajagopal were among those who spoke.

World.title: Slipper hurled at MP Pappu Yadav; Opposition slams police
World.content:
Two men intruded into the residence of Independent MP Pappu Yadav on Sunday (August 2, 2026) and one of them hurled a slipper at him when he was addressing a press conference.

While his supporters alleged that one assailant was also carrying a knife, Opposition leaders targeted the Delhi police for failing to ensure the safety of a parliamentarian.

At the press conference, Mr. Yadav countered the allegations levelled against him for staging a skit on the Ram Temple donation theft in the Parliament complex on July 31.

Referring to the donations case, Mr. Yadav said he had only asked questions about the missing gold and silver. “I have done nothing wrong. It is not as if I am not a Sanatani. Today, we are demanding answers from the Prime Minister regarding the way the faith of the common man has been undermined,” he said.

The incident took place around 6.15 p.m. Standing among the journalists, one of the intruders – later identified as Sumit from Uttar Pradesh’s Bulandshahr – hurled a footwear at Mr. Yadav, following which his supporters overpowered him. The police later took him into custody.

Mr. Yadav later told mediapersons: “There has been an ongoing conspiracy to kill me. Several babas have spoken about ‘burning me alive or killing me’ ...had so many people not been present, I would have been dead today. Just last night, my family was also harassed.”

On the Varanasi police registering a first information report against him, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, and Samajwadi Party MP Awadhesh Prasad [for the skit], he said: “Rahul Gandhi was never afraid of an FIR; Priyanka Gandhi was never afraid; so how could Pappu Yadav be afraid? If Pappu Yadav has to die to protest the faith of the people of Sanatan and India against those who betray Sanatan and God, I [will] step out every day to face death…”

Major failure, says advocate

In a statement to the media, Mr. Yadav’s advocate Kanishk Arora termed it a major failure of the police, particularly when they were told a day earlier that there was the possibility of anti-social elements resorting to such an act. “Despite informing the police, only two or three personnel were deployed. Even then, this incident occurred, which I strongly condemn. We will initiate legal action,” he said.

The incident provoked sharp reactions from Opposition leaders. Congress MP Pawan Khera criticised the police. “The Delhi police seems remarkably efficient when it comes to repressing students peacefully demanding their constitutional rights. But when it comes to protecting a vocal Opposition leader – even a sitting Member of Parliament – at his own residence, it suddenly falls short,” he said.

He said: “Even since Anurag Kumar took charge as Delhi’s Police Commissioner, the force’s record has gone from bad to worse.”

CPI (M) MP V. Sivadasan also condemned the attack, saying that those who raised questions about the alleged loot of the temple’s money or the money donated by believers were facing attacks by “RSS and BJP persons”. He said huge amounts had been looted allegedly by the members of trust, which was formed by the Modi government. The BJP was also in power in Uttar Pradesh. He alleged that the Union government had been using Central enforcement agencies against the Opposition and now “goons” were also working for them.

Condemning the incident, Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, however, urged Mr. Yadav to desist from making “provocative” statements. “There is no place for aggressive politics, but if you attack Sanatan dharma, if you condemn religious beliefs, there is going to be a backlash. Nobody is propagating violence, but this attack on democracy and public representatives needs to be condemned unequivocally. Pappu Yadav should also think why he makes such kind of provocative statements that attracts reactions in this particular way,” she said.

Rajya Sabha MP Upendra Kushwaha also denounced the incident. “There is no place for such actions in a democracy. The way Pappu Yadav himself has been conducting himself is objectionable. But, regardless of that, whoever threw the slipper, it is unacceptable,” he said.

Mr. Sumit’s friend Happy Sharma, later told the media that he and Sumit had come from Bulandshahr to Mr. Yadav’s residence to support the sadhus protesting against the MP for "hurting their religious sentiments”. “We only asked him why he was insulting the sadhus and saints, saffron robes, and Lord Ram...slippers were thrown only after they assaulted us...We have done nothing wrong and will do it again if the country’s sadhus, saints, and Lord Ram are insulted, whatever be the consequence,” he said.

The police are yet to issue an official statement on the incident.

(with inputs from agencies)

World.title: At least 14 people, including police officials, martyred in suicide attack on Kabal police station in Swat: police
World.content:
At least 14 people, including police officials, were martyred and at least 18 others injured in a suicide attack on Swat’s Kabal police station on Sunday, police and rescue officials said.

Swat police spokesperson Nasir Iqbal Karimi, while speaking to Dawn, confirmed the death toll.

Malakand Division Deputy Inspector General of Police Fida Hussain told AFP that police officers were among those martyred.

He added that another body, suspected to be that of the bomber, had been brought to the hospital.

According to the Swat District Police Officer (DPO) Umar Khan, the suicide bomber detonated explosives after police personnel attempted to stop and search him at the entrance of the police station.

The DPO said that the police remained on high alert. “Security forces have cordoned off the area, and an investigation is underway to collect further evidence,“ he added.

The explosion occurred near the gate of Kabal police station while hundreds of people were participating in a public demonstration at nearby Kabal Chowk against the recent wave of terrorism in Swat Valley.

Police officials inspect the site following a suicide bombing during a protest in Swat district on August 2. — AFP

The bodies of nine victims were shifted to Central Hospital Saidu Sharif, while the bodies of five others were moved to Kabal Hospital, where doctors confirmed their deaths, said Rescue 1122 Spokesperson Bilal Ahmed Faizi.

The spokesperson added that two of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.

The powerful blast caused multiple casualties, prompting an immediate emergency response from police, rescue teams and local authorities. Security personnel also sealed off the area and launched a search operation.

The protest had drawn a large crowd from across the district and the attack occurred as the final speaker was addressing the crowd, triggering panic among participants. No group has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Addressing the gathering before the blast, the speakers condemned the resurgence of terrorism in Swat and demanded that the government ensure lasting peace. They said their movement had a single agenda: the restoration of peace and the elimination of terrorism from the region.

The speakers stressed that maintaining law and order and eradicating terrorism were the state’s responsibility, warning that continued insecurity could trigger widespread public unrest, citing recent protest movements in other countries as examples of growing public frustration.

The speakers also criticised the authorities for what they described as action against peaceful citizens while terrorists continued to operate in the mountainous areas of Swat. They alleged that terrorists had openly circulated videos on social media and questioned why stronger action had not been taken against them.

“Our children deserve education, and our families deserve to live in peace,” one speaker told the gathering.

“We have witnessed years of bloodshed. Our mothers, sisters, and daughters have suffered immensely, and we do not want another generation of widows and orphans.”

Condemnations pour in

President Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the loss of life and called for a comprehensive investigation into the incident, according to a statement issued by his office on X.

President Zardari directed the relevant authorities to provide the best possible medical facilities to those injured.

“Terrorists will never succeed in their nefarious efforts to undermine peace, national unity and the writ of the state,” he was quoted as saying. He added that the sacrifices of the KP police were “a source of pride for the entire nation”.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also condemned the blast.

“Terrorists cannot demoralise the nation with cowardly attacks,” Kundi was quoted as saying, as per a statement.

KP Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, condemning the incident, sought a report from the KP Inspector General of Police (IGP) and offered condolences to the families of the deceased.

“The elements hostile to peace will never be allowed to succeed in their nefarious intentions,” the chief minister was quoted as saying.

Earlier in the day, an IED blast near the Peshawar-Islamabad motorway toll plaza injured two policemen in the provincial capital Peshawar. On July 30, a terrorist attack on a police checkpost in Hangu martyred nine policemen.

KP has seen an uptick in terrorist activity. According to the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies’s monthly security assessment, KP, excluding the merged districts, recorded 154 terrorism related deaths in July, compared with 75 in June, representing an increase of 105 per cent.

World.title: Second phase of AJK polls concludes amid renewed rigging allegations by PPP
World.content:
The second phase of the Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK) elections took place on Sunday, with polling held in eight out of the nine constituencies of Muzaffarabad division and all 12 refugee constituencies.

Polling began at 8am and continued till 5pm for the refugee seats, while the process concluded at 6pm in Muzaffarabad after an hour-long extension.

The electoral process in LA-27 (Muzaffarabad-I) was postponed due to heavy rain, AJK Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal said, DawnNewsTV reported.

Polling in LA-27, commonly known as Kutla, was deferred until August 4 after polling material could not be dispatched due to a landslide.

Similarly, polling in 52 of the 147 polling stations of LA-28 (Muzaffarabad-II) was also postponed until August 4 for the same reason.

Over 300 candidates were in the fray for the Muzaffarabad seats and the 12 seats for refugees settled in different regions.

Continuing his rigging allegations, PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari on Sunday accused the PML-N of “robbing” votes in the second phase of the AJK elections as well.

In a post on X later in the day, he condemned an “attack” on the party’s regional president, Chaudhry Latif Akbar — also the candidate for LA-31 (Muzaffarabad-V).

Accusing “miscreant elements of the PML-N” of being behind the incident, Bilawal said PPP worker Mushtaq Shah was killed in the same constituency.

“The PML-N is robbing the votes of the people of Azad Kashmir through bullets, batons and coercion,” he alleged.

The PPP chairman demanded that those responsible for the attack on Akbar and the “murderers” of the party worker be arrested immediately.

In a separate statement, Bilawal said, “The PML-N has crossed all limits. Attacks are taking place on our voters and the president of the state (AJK).”

He remarked that in Muzaffarabad, the PPP’s “politics of dignity and principles was in contest with the PML-N’s threat, rigging and coercion”.

The PPP shared a complaint written to the Election Commission regarding a “physical assault” on Akbar.

The party said the LA-31 candidate was “engaged in the electoral process on polling day” when the alleged incident took place, accusing three individuals.

It said a first information report (FIR) was being registered and urged the Election Commission to order an inquiry into the “security lapse” that resulted in the incident.

AJK Prime Minister Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, who belongs to the PPP, took notice of the incident and ordered the chief secretary and the police chief to take those responsible to justice.

The AJK PM termed the attack “a slap on the politics of dignity and principle in Kashmir”.

Akbar also wrote two letters to the Election Commission. In one, he alleged that an attempt on his life was made at Polling Station 177 “by PML-N workers” and wrote of the PPP worker’s death.

He further claimed that his polling agents were not allowed to “sit in the polling area” at 14 polling stations.

In the second letter, Akbar said PPP leader Syed Mumtaz Hussain Naqvi sustained bullet wounds in a “[murderous] attack” at a polling station in a building.

Addressing a press conference, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari claimed that eight party workers had been injured in the ongoing elections so far.

Bokhari contended there was a “state of lawlessness” in AJK.

Polls in AJK are being held in three phases over security concerns, with the first set of polls held in Mirpur division on July 27, the second held today, and the third phase set for August 10 across Poonch division.

Ahead of today’s elections, internet services were restored in parts of Muzaffarabad division after remaining suspended for 54 days on July 29. At the time, it was not clear whether the restoration covered the entire division or was limited to the state capital.

Addressing the media on Sunday, the AJK CEC said that a letter had been written yesterday to request the restoration of internet services.

He added that the outcome would be known today, without providing further details.

“We will work according to the law; we will not come under pressure from anyone,” CEC Mughal said to a question.

Preliminary, unofficial results

According to preliminary and unofficial results, the PML-N was leading in LA-25 by 1,364 votes, while the PPP was ahead in LA-26 and LA-28 by 1,745 and 1,782 votes, respectively.

In LA-29, the PML-N was leading by 379 votes, with the PPP in second place. Similarly, the PML-N was ahead in LA-30 by 247 votes, while the PPP was trailing in second position.

In LA-31, the PML-N was leading with 2,934 votes, while the PPP was in second place. In LA-32, the PML-N was ahead by 892 votes, according to the unofficial results.

In LA-33, the PPP was leading by 1,349 votes, while the PML-N was ahead in LA-34 with a lead of 2,503 votes.

Refugee seats
